https://www.hertie-school.org/en/news/de.text: Press release 22.09.2026 Daniela Schwarzer to become new Hertie School President Duration : 4:53 min The political scientist and internationally renowned expert on European and international affairs will take over as president of the Berlin-based university for governance on 1 November 2026. Daniela Schwarzer will begin her term as the new President of the Hertie School in Berlin on 1 November 2026. She succeeds Cornelia Woll, who served as president until March 2026. In accordance with the Hertie School’s statutes, the new president’s initial term will run for four years, until 2030. In addition to serving as president, Daniela Schwarzer will take up a professorship in European Governance and Geopolitics at the Hertie School on 1 November 2026. Daniela Schwarzer’s official appointment follows an international selection process and final approval by internal and external bodies, in accordance with the Hertie School’s statutes and the Berlin Higher Education Act. “We are delighted with the appointment of Daniela Schwarzer. Her reputation and recognized expertise in international politics, academia and the foundation sector will be an enormous asset to the Hertie School,” says Helge Braun , Chair of the Search Committee and Chair of the Hertie School Board of Trustees. “With this outstanding appointment, we are setting the course for a successful future for the Hertie School. We very much look forward to working with Daniela Schwarzer to further develop the Hertie School and strengthen its position as a leading institution for research and teaching on good governance,” says Frank Mattern , Chair of the Hertie School Supervisory Board. The Hertie School: A leading institution for politics and good governance The Hertie School was founded in 2004 by the Hertie Foundation as a private university for good governance and has since established itself as a leading institution for research, teaching and public debate in political science and public administration. The university ranks among the top institutions in Europe and Germany in numerous rankings, including in the latest QS World University Rankings . Around 900 students from more than 70 countries are currently enrolled at the Hertie School. At the start of the current academic year in September 2026, the university welcomed more than 400 new students – the largest incoming class in its history. From February 2027, the Hertie School will move to its new campus at the historic Robert Koch Forum in Berlin’s government district. For more information about our new campus, visit this page: Our new campus . About Daniela Schwarzer Prof. Dr Daniela Schwarzer is a political scientist and one of Germany’s leading experts on European and international affairs. From 2023 to June 2026, she served on the Executive Board of the Bertelsmann Stiftung, where she led the programs Europe’s Future and Democracy and Cohesion. Daniela Schwarzer is Honorary President of the Institut für Auslandsbeziehungen (ifa). Before joining the Bertelsmann Stiftung, she was Executive Director for Europe and Central Asia at the Open Society Foundations and Director and CEO of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP). Earlier in her career, she held leadership positions at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP) and the German Marshall Fund of the United States. Daniela Schwarzer is an honorary professor of political science at Freie Universität Berlin and a Senior Fellow at Harvard University. She regularly advises governments and international institutions on European integration, foreign and security policy. Among other roles, she served as co-rapporteur of the Franco-German expert group on EU institutional reform and enlargement in 2023 and as Special Advisor to Josep Borrell, then High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy and Vice-President of the European Commission, from 2020 to 2022. Press contact Benjamin Stappenbeck, Director of Communications, Hertie School +49 (0) 30 259 219 – 113 [email protected]

https://www.sprind.org/en/actions/challe.text: Apply now Your Challenge: AI-Native Chip Design Topic Goal Participate Webinar FAQ Contact Hello, innovators! Chip design is complex, expensive, and takes years, while AI models emerge in just weeks. We need pioneering teams for whom speed is everything. Teams that make tomorrow’s chip development as effortless as today’s software engineering. We need you. COMPRESSING CHIP DESIGN FROM YEARS TO WEEKS Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping every sector, from medicine and mobility to energy and data security. What is considered an innovation today becomes standard tomorrow. The pace of development accelerates week after week. Yet, while the AI landscape transforms on a daily basis, hardware is failing to keep up. The chips meant to power our AI systems are designed for yesterday's models. The scaling rules that defined semiconductor development for decades no longer apply. Instead, the path of innovation is shifting toward novel approaches and visionary architectures beyond legacy systems. The opportunity: Emerging AI models and open-source technologies are lowering entry barriers, enabling design possibilities that were unthinkable just a short time ago. The innovation space is expanding. That is why we are convinced: Now is the time for a strategic fresh start in chip design – Made in Europe. A collaborative project by the European innovation agencies SPRIND and NADI (National Agency for Disruptive Innovation), which is currently being established in the Netherlands. Play video Allow data transfer to/from vimeo.com? (learn more) The Challenge: Designing high-efficiency AI Chips in weeks, not in years – with AI-Native Systems. The goal of this Challenge is to leverage AI to drastically shorten the design process of high-performance chips and develop concrete, production-ready chip designs tailored for AI applications. From architecture search to RTL generation and verification, AI systems are expected to autonomously drive and optimize the development workflow. Reinforcement learning and autonomous agent systems will enable independent decision-making across complex design trade-offs, compressing timelines from years to weeks. AI becomes the actual chip designer. We are calling for high-performance, energy-efficient chip architectures built specifically for the demands of AI Giga-Factories and European core strengths such as data security, biotechnology, robotics, and mobility. The goal is to set new benchmarks in compute power, energy efficiency, and scalability. We support: Potential breakthrough innovations The Challenge spans 20 months across two stages. https://www.bmftr.bund.de/SharedDocs/Bek.text: 22.09.2026 - 30.11.2026 Bekanntmachung Richtlinie zur Förderung von Projekten zum Thema „Innovative Herstellung von E-Fuels und CCU-basierten Vorprodukten – Neue Wege für klimaneutrale Kraftstoffe der Zukunft“, Bundesanzeiger vom 22.09.2026 Vom 10. September 2026 1 Förderziel, Zuwendungszweck, Rechtsgrundlage Die nationalen und europäischen Klimaziele sowie das Bundes-Klimaschutzgesetz sehen eine weitgehende Reduktion der Treibhausgasemissionen bis hin zur Netto-Treibhausgasneutralität im Jahr 2045 vor. Dafür sind der Ausbau erneuerbarer Energien und die Elektrifizierung fossiler Prozesse in Industrie, Mobilität und Wärme zentrale Voraussetzungen. Vor diesem Hintergrund gewinnen klimafreundliche E-Fuels zunehmend an Bedeutung. So sind insbesondere die Luft- und Schifffahrt sowie Sonder- und Spezialfahrzeuge und der militärische Bereich aufgrund hoher Anforderungen an Energiedichte, Reichweite, Speicherfähigkeit sowie Resilienz auch langfristig auf flüssige oder gasförmige Energieträger angewiesen. Für ihre Herstellung wird nachhaltiger Kohlenstoff benötigt, der neben biogenen Quellen auch aus der Atmosphäre mittels Direct Air Capture bereitgestellt werden kann. Darüber hinaus stellt auch die Nutzung von schwer vermeidbarem CO2 aus industriellen Punktquellen eine Möglichkeit für Emissionsreduktionen dar. Durch die Nutzung dieser CO2-Quellen können weitestgehend klimaneutrale E-Fuels produziert werden. Beispielsweise spielt Methanol dabei eine wichtige Rolle, sowohl als klimafreundlicher Kraftstoff und Energieträger zur Speicherung und zum Transport erneuerbarer Energie als auch als Ausgangsstoff für weitere E-Fuels wie Sustainable Aviation Fuels. E-Fuels bieten somit eine skalierbare Lösung für schwer elektrifizierbare Mobilitätssegmente und sind zugleich weitgehend kompatibel mit bestehenden Infrastrukturen. Die Hightech Agenda Deutschland (HTAD) adressiert diese Herausforderungen gezielt und hebt klimafreundliche Kraftstoffe innerhalb der Schlüsseltechnologie „Technologien für die klimaneutrale Mobilität“ hervor. Ziel ist es, Deutschland als Forschungs-, Entwicklungs- und Technologiestandort für E-Fuels zu stärken sowie internationale Märkte aktiv vorzubereiten und mitzugestalten. Mit dieser Maßnahme zum Thema innovative Herstellung von E-Fuels und dafür gegebenenfalls notwendige CCU (Carbon Capture and Utilization)-basierte Vorprozessketten sollen bestehende Hemmnisse überwunden, Forschung und Entwicklung intensiviert und die Grundlage für eine spätere industrielle Demonstration gelegt werden. Vor diesem Hintergrund startet das Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) mit dieser Förderrichtlinie die Forschungs- und Entwicklungsförderung „Innovative Herstellung von E-Fuels und CCU-basierten Vorprodukten – Neue Wege für klimaneutrale Kraftstoffe der Zukunft“. Diese soll deutlich intensiviert werden, um einen beschleunigten Beitrag zur klimaneutralen Mobilität sowie zur Stärkung der technologischen Wettbewerbsfähigkeit Deutschlands zu leisten. 1.1 Förderziel Die vorliegende Fördermaßnahme zielt darauf ab, Deutschland als führenden Forschungs- und Entwicklungsstandort für Technologien zur Herstellung klimafreundlicher, strom- und wasserstoffbasierter E-Fuels, auch auf Basis von CCU, in Europa weiter zu stärken und perspektivisch als globalen Leitanbieter und bedeutenden Technologieexporteur zu positionieren. Hierzu sollen innovative Verfahren, Prozesse und Technologien zu E-Fuels und, falls erforderlich, zu CCU-basierten Vorprodukten untersucht werden. Ziel sind Anwendungen zur Defossilisierung des Luft- und Schiffsverkehrs sowie weiterer Mobilitäts- und Transportsegmente mit besonderen Anforderungen an E-Fuels und klimaneutrale Kraftstoffe. Im Bereich kohlenstoffbasierter E-Fuel-Vorprodukte aus CCU soll dabei perspektivisch auf die Nutzung nachhaltiger Kohlenstoffquellen fokussiert werden. Darüber hinaus können ebenfalls schwer vermeidbare CO2-Emissionen wie bei der Kalk-, Stahl- und Zementherstellung sowie Reststoffverwertung adressiert werden. Neuartige Ansätze müssen identifiziert und grundlegende Innovationen vorangetrieben werden, um in wettbewerbsfähige Lösungen von übermorgen zu münden. Darüber hinaus zielt die Förderrichtlinie darauf ab, technologische Innovationen mit nachweislich signifikanten Verbesserungen gegenüber dem Stand von Wissenschaft und Technik zu generieren, neuartige Lösungsansätze mit klarer Skalierungs- und Anwendungsperspektive zu entwickeln, den Wissens- und Technologietransfer zwischen Wissenschaft, Wirtschaft und weiteren Innovationsakteuren zu beschleunigen, die Grundlage für die internationale Wettbewerbsfähigkeit der deutschen Industrie, insbesondere von kleinen und mittleren Unternehmen (KMU) und Zulieferern, zu legen und die Voraussetzungen für zukünftige Wertschöpfung und Exportpotenziale der innovativen Technologien im Bereich E-Fuels und dazugehöriger CCU-Technologien zu schaffen. Die Förderziele sind erreicht, wenn durch die geförderten Vorhabe

https://die-ngo-debatte-podcast.podigee..text: Shownotes In dieser Folge sprechen Victoria Strachwitz und Michael Seberich mit Annette Schavan, Vorstandsvorsitzende der Hertie Stiftung, ehemalige Bundesbildungsministerin und Botschafterin darüber, wie Demokratiebildung aussieht und wer sie alles leistet. Nach einem genaueren Blick auf Stiftungsarbeit, blicken sie auf die Zivilgesellschaft als Akteurin, sowie aktuelle politische Geschehnisse und die Frage, wie wir unsere Demokratie erhalten. Unsere Argumentationshilfen: „Demokratie lernt man in der Schule.“ Schule spielt dabei eine zentrale Rolle. Demokratie entsteht aber nicht nur im Klassenzimmer, sondern überall dort, wo Menschen Verantwortung übernehmen, diskutieren, Kompromisse finden und sich für andere engagieren: im Verein, im Ehrenamt, in der Familie oder im Alltag. Entscheidend ist also das Zusammenspiel von Schule und Zivilgesellschaft: Demokratie muss nicht nur vermittelt, sondern auch erlebt und praktiziert werden. „Demokratieförderung ist allein Aufgabe des Staates.“ Der Staat trägt hier selbstverständlich Verantwortung. Eine lebendige Demokratie lebt aber genauso von Stiftungen, Vereinen, Initiativen und engagierten Bürgerinnen und Bürgern. Gerade dieser vorpolitische Raum ist wichtig, weil dort demokratische Erfahrungen gesammelt werden, lange bevor Menschen vielleicht selbst politisch aktiv werden. Demokratieförderung ist deshalb eine gemeinsame Aufgabe von Staat und Zivilgesellschaft. „NGOs sollten sich aus Politik heraushalten.“ Zivilgesellschaft lebt davon, dass Menschen ihre Anliegen vertreten und in gesellschaftliche Debatten einbringen. NGOs können wichtige Debatten anstoßen und politische Diskurse vorbereiten, die später auch in die Politik einfließen. Entscheidend ist deshalb nicht, ob sie sich politisch äußern, sondern wie: transparent, demokratisch und im Rahmen der freiheitlichen Ordnung. Dabei sollte man zwischen politisch und parteipolitisch unterscheiden: Zivilgesellschaft sollte nicht parteipolitisch sein und kann trotzdem dabei politisch sein. Sie darf Positionen vertreten, Debatten anstoßen und gesellschaftliche Veränderungen anregen. Genau darin liegt ihre wichtige Funktion als Debatten- und Erfahrungsraum unserer Demokratie. https://www.sprind.org/en/actions/challe.text: 1st stage of the Funke Funke QuantumSense Exploration Topic Goal Teams Jury FAQ Contact Hello people with radical new ideas. We need breakthrough innovations to redefine the boundaries of quantum sensing. We need new ways of thinking to unlock novel measurement methods and quantum systems. We need bold ideas. We need you. The foundations of quantum sensing are well understood. Quantum effects can be deliberately harnessed to perform measurements with previously unreachable precision. Yet despite the enormous progress in the field, today’s quantum sensing technologies still use only a small fraction of the potentially available quantum systems and measurement methods. Only a small portion of the theoretically conceivable space has been explored technologically. The true potential of quantum sensing is therefore far from exhausted. This is exactly where this SPRIND Funke comes in. We want to open up this still largely unexplored space. We are looking for radically new approaches to make new quantum systems and measurement methods usable for quantum sensing. Quantum Sensing Initiative What is emerging today in quantum technology could transform entire industries tomorrow. The potential is growing to fundamentally redefine the limits of what is possible. We believe quantum sensing is one of the fields with the greatest potential for breakthrough innovation. That is why the Read more The challenge: To develop novel methods to identify and leverage new quantum sensors or quantum systems suitable for sensing applications more rapidly, systematically, and at greater scale. In this SPRIND Funke, teams are invited to open up new pathways for harnessing previously unused quantum effects, quantum systems, or measurement principles for sensing applications. The focus is not on optimizing already known sensor types, but on discovering entirely new quantum systems that can be used for sensing. We are looking for approaches that go beyond the current state of the art and create entirely new technological possibilities. Possible approaches could include AI-supported exploration based on physical simulations or the systematic, AI-assisted analysis of cross-disciplinary scientific literature. The goal may be to identify new molecules with highly readable quantum states, unlock alternative quantum systems, or develop novel measurement concepts that significantly simplify existing applications or enable entirely new ones. Teams are free to define their own transformative approach. We are not looking for incremental improvements, but for exploratory approaches with the potential to fundamentally expand the technological foundations of quantum sensing. We support: potential breakthrough innovations Teams participating in this Funke are fully challenged. SPRIND therefore provides intensive and individual support. This includes funding of up to €450,000 in Stage 1 and up to €150,000 in Stage 2. In order to help the teams develop their full potential, SPRIND provides them not only with financial support but also with individual mentoring, networking opportunities, and coaching. To enable teams to focus entirely on their innovations, funding is provided quickly and with minimal bureaucracy. Stage 1 will begin on September 20, 2026, with up to seven teams. After five months, the jury will decide which teams, up to a maximum of five, will continue for an additional two months. The challenge will run for a total duration of seven months. The goal is to make bold ideas visible in a short period of time, identify technological potential at an early stage, and activate the ecosystem. Taking it one step further: Ideas with breakthrough innovation potential must ultimately reach real-world application in order to create impact. That is why promising projects may continue to receive SPRIND support even beyond the challenge itself. https://www.sprind.org/en/actions/challe.text: 1st stage of the Funke Funke Quantum-Driven Intelligence Topic Goal Teams Jury FAQ Contact Hello people with radical new ideas! We need breakthrough innovations that take quantum sensing one step further. We need quantum sensing that does not just measure, but understands. We need bold ideas. We need you. Quantum sensors promise a new era of measurement technology. They provide data with previously unreachable precision. But precision alone is not enough. The real value emerges when this data is combined with additional information sources to generate entirely new insights. That is what we are aiming for: connecting high-precision quantum sensor data with existing data sources, models, and sensor systems in order to unlock previously inaccessible, decision-relevant information. The possibilities range from geological and satellite-based applications to climate, infrastructure, and security systems. Another promising approach is the enhancement of existing classical sensor systems - for example in autonomous driving - through the integration of quantum sensing. Quantum Sensing Initiative What is emerging today in quantum technology could transform entire industries tomorrow. The potential is growing to fundamentally redefine the limits of what is possible. We believe quantum sensing is one of the fields with the greatest potential for breakthrough innovation. That is why the Read more The challenge: to develop practical applications or scenarios in which the integration of quantum sensing significantly improves existing systems, models, or analytical methods and delivers substantial added value. In this SPRIND Funke, teams are invited to develop use cases in which quantum sensing fundamentally enhances existing systems. Both real and simulated quantum sensor data may be used. The goal is to demonstrate the added value quantum sensing can generate in specific scenarios — for example through higher precision, improved predictions, more robust navigation, or entirely new forms of data analysis. Teams are free to define their own transformative use case. The goal is to uncover applications that would not be feasible - or would be significantly less powerful - without quantum sensing. At the same time, the developed approaches should help derive tangible requirements for future quantum sensing technologies, particularly regarding necessary measurement accuracy, integrability, and suitable deployment scenarios. In this way, the Funke will not only deepen the understanding of potential applications, but also establish a robust foundation for the next generation of quantum sensing technologies. We support: potential breakthrough innovations Teams participating in this Funke are fully challenged. SPRIND therefore provides intensive and individual support. This includes funding of up to €200,000 in Stage 1 and up to €100,000 in Stage 2. In order to help the teams develop their full potential, SPRIND provides them not only with financial support but also with individual mentoring, networking opportunities, and coaching. To enable teams to focus entirely on their innovations, funding is provided quickly and with minimal bureaucracy. Stage 1 will begin on September 20, 2026, with up to 15 teams. After four months, the jury will decide which teams, up to a maximum of ten, will continue for an additional two months. The Funke will run for a total duration of six months. The goal is to make bold ideas visible in a short period of time, identify technological potential at an early stage, and activate the ecosystem. Taking it one step further: Ideas with breakthrough innovation potential must ultimately reach real-world application in order to create impact. That is why promising projects may continue to receive SPRIND support even beyond the Funke itself. https://www.sprind.org/en/actions/challe.text: Funke completed Funke Next Frontier AI Concepts Topic Goal Teams FAQ Contact Hello innovators! We need visionary concepts for Frontier AI Labs that push the algorithmic boundaries of today and strengthen Europe’s sovereignty – disruptive, scalable, evolving. We need bold ideas. We need you. Frontier AI labs in the USA and China are setting the standards, while Europe remains dependent. Large models dominate, and disruptive approaches such as hybrid architectures or agent-based systems remain untapped. Without strategic autonomy in AI, Europe cannot catch up in the pursuit of innovation leadership. The Next Frontier AI Initiative closes this gap. The SPRIND Funke Next Frontier AI Concepts is the first of several innovation competitions within the initiative and calls for the design of new Frontier AI labs. The goal is not the incremental development of existing models; instead, creative approaches are sought that redefine the frontier and coherently integrate research, prototyping, and deployment – with a clear go-to-market mindset and operational excellence. The Funke functions as an early-stage financing bridge for Frontier AI teams in advance of the SPRIND NFAI Challenge. Its role is to sustain high-potential teams until the Challenge opens in July 2026, ensuring continuity of work and safeguarding against attrition of critical talent. The challenge: to develop independent, visionary concepts within just a few months that will serve as the foundation for a European Frontier AI Lab in the future. We are looking for disruptive model architectures, modalities, training paradigms, or multi-agent systems – an adaptive concept that addresses a clear research domain, demonstrates its uniqueness compared to existing solutions, and strengthens European sovereignty. We expect a theoretical foundation, a realistic roadmap for further development, and a sign of life demonstrating that the core innovation works, is scalable, and strategically significant. Teams of the second stage The World Model for Molecular Biology Learn more <!--[--><!--]--> Efficient online synthesis of world models Learn more <!--[--><!--]--> We support: potential breakthrough innovations The SPRIND Funke spans five months and is structured in two stages. A jury of internationally recognized experts assists SPRIND in evaluating the applications and selects up to six teams to participate in Stage 1. Teams participating in this Funke will be pushed to their full potential. SPRIND provides individualized support at every stage of the Spark, including financial backing and direct access to a network of experts and potential collaborators. For Stage 1, teams can receive up to €200,000 (plus VAT). After each stage, the jury reviews interim results and evaluates which teams demonstrate the greatest breakthrough innovation potential. https://www.sprind.org/en/actions/challe.text: Funke completed Funke Anti-Drone Response Challenge Teams FAQ Contact Hello people with radical new ideas! We need breakthrough innovation to define a new era of airspace security – intelligent, autonomous, and non-destructive. We need bold ideas. We need you. Small and micro drones have become part of modern conflicts – and a growing risk to civilian safety. They are fast, low-cost, hard to detect – and often autonomous. Whether in war zones, over stadiums, or at airports: their uses range from surveillance to sabotage. Existing defense systems? Overwhelmed. The SPRIND Funke Anti-Drone Response closes this gap and calls for a paradigm shift: What is needed are non-destructive, scalable and fully autonomous defense solutions that reliably detect threats, react quickly and neutralize drones without endangering the surrounding airspace or any third parties. The goal is not the kinetic flight-system destruction but mitigation by means of intelligent effects, diversion, blockade or other reversible measures. The challenge: To develop a fully autonomous system that can detect, classify, and neutralize small and micro UAVs in real time – without weapons, external communication, or human intervention. What we're looking for: an adaptive, integrated system that identifies threats, classifies them reliably, and responds with non-kinetic, reversible measures – such as capture, redirection, or blocking. The solution must prove itself in realistic scenarios and offer strong dual-use potential for civil and military contexts. SPRIND Funke Anti-Drone Response ended after stage 1 The SPRIND Funke program launched on August 15 and was planned to run for a total of almost four months in two stages. SPRIND offered successful teams up to EUR 67,000 and a one-time test setting for the entire duration of the program. However, following the live demonstrations at the end of the first stage in September 2025, the expert jury decided to end the initiative after the first stage, as the milestones set in stage 1 were not achieved by enough teams to continue. The theme of the SPRIND Spark, Anti-Drone Response, remains highly relevant. Even if projects are not always continued in their originally planned form, each phase offers learning opportunities that drive long-term progress. SPRIND supports innovators who are pushing the boundaries of science and technology in further Challenges and Funken. https://www.sprind.org/en/actions/challe.text: Funke completed Funke Deepfake DETECTION AND PREVENTION Topic Goal The winners The Jury Further Teams Contact Hello, innovators! We need breakthrough innovations in the fight against deepfakes to ensure the integrity of our digital world. We need bold ideas. We found them. They imitate voices, distort identities, and undermine our trust in digital images: Deepfakes have long been more than just an internet phenomenon. They are a systemic challenge for the media, politics, business, and each and every one of us. With the SPRIND Funke Deepfake Detection & Prevention, we searched for new, bold answers to this very problem. Play video Allow data transfer to/from vimeo.com? (learn more) The task: Develop a prototype that reliably detects deepfakes images from various media content and/or protects existing infrastructures from the use of deepfakes with preventive measures. Over a period of 13 months, up to twelve teams worked on prototypes that redefine digital authenticity. The conditions were challenging: The teams received individual funding of up to €725,000 over two stages, access to expertise from research, regulation, and industry, and continuous sparring from SPRIND. The goal was to develop a functional prototype that not only detects deepfakes but also enables authenticatable, trustworthy image content – scalable, robust, and flexible in its application. During this time, teams tested, discarded, rethought, and refined their ideas. Deepfake techniques changed, models became more complex, and playback methods more diverse. At the end of November 2025, the renowned jury met for the third time and selected the winner of SPRIND Funke from the seven remaining teams in the second stage. The winners The Cinematic Context Aware AI Image Detection approach (itsreal.media) developed by director Christoph Behl's team convinced with its combination of precise technical analysis and a holistic view of the image, including hundreds of visual and structural patterns. This was complemented by the use of powerful deep learning models and a flexible, highly adaptive meta-model that can be quickly adapted to new models and feature sets. In addition, the team achieved the highest recognition rates for both fully generated AI images and the correct identification of authentic ( real-as-real ) images. https://www.sprind.org/en/actions/challe.text: Funke completed Funke EUDI WALLET Prototypes Topic Goal Teams Jury Conference FAQ Contact Hello people with radical new ideas! We need pioneering solutions to shape the future of digital identity in Germany. Digital proof of identity is an important basis for the digitalization of our lives. Digital wallets enable users to receive, manage, and present proof of identity and other documentation as part of digital processes. This will make digital wallets an essential part of our society’s digital infrastructure. They will enable the complete digitalization of processes and thus allow for completely new approaches to problems, which also makes them the basis for disruptive innovations. The goal of the Funke Challenge was to develop and test technical solutions for future German EUDI Wallets in the form of prototypes. It was an innovation competition that generated valuable insights, which have been incorporated into the development of secure, privacy-preserving, user-friendly, and widely adoptable EUDI Wallets. The participating teams developed prototypes for a trustworthy, intuitive, and universally applicable European Digital Identity Wallet for users in the Federal Republic of Germany. SPRIND Funke successfully completed The SPRIND Funke EUDI Wallet Prototypes challenge ran for 15 months across three stages. In Stage 1, SPRIND funded six teams; in Stage 2, four teams; and in Stage 3, two teams. During Stage 1, each selected team received up to €300,000 in funding, and in Stage 2, up to €300,000 each as well. For Stage 3, the two finalist teams received up to €450,000 each. The second and third stages were accompanied by the LSP POTENTIAL. The third conference in October 2025 marked the official conclusion of the Funke innovation challenge. Interested visitors had the opportunity to get to know the eleven Funke teams and test their EUDI Wallet prototypes on site. In addition, the stage program offered exciting expert talks and panel discussions. The documentation of the event is available at openCode . The second Funke Conference The second Funke EUDI Wallet Prototypes conference took place in Berlin on December 11, 2024. Eight international teams worked on the further development of their innovative prototypes in stage 2. In the end, 4 teams made it to the final 3rd stage and were announced at the end of the conference. The documentation of the second Funke conference is available on openCode . The third Funke Conference On October 14, 2025 , the third and final Funke Conference EUDI Wallet Prototypes took place in Berlin. Four international teams worked in Stage 3 on advancing their innovative prototypes. After months of development, the four remaining teams presented their EUDI Wallet prototypes. The focus was on practical use cases, new technical approaches, and the shared ambition to combine security, data protection, and user experience. The conference showcased the remarkable innovative strength of Europe’s tech and identity community – and how ideas are turning into tangible solutions for the future EUDI Wallet ecosystem. We need pioneering solutions to shape the mobility and logistics of the future with the help of autonomous aerial vehicles. We need you. Logistics and mobility are the basis for a flourishing economy and society. In light of demographic change, the declining number of skilled workers and the simultaneously high and ever growing demands on passenger and freight transport, shaping the mobility of the future appears to be one of the key challenges of the 21st century. Unmanned, largely manually controlled aerial vehicles are already an important addition in many areas of application such as the delivery of goods, the maintenance of industrial plants, in surveying technology or even in fire protection and rescue operations. The private as well as the commercial use of drones has been increasing continuously for years. Unmanned aircraft systems will profoundly change future transport. However, the safe operation of autonomous systems still remains challenging - especially under changing environmental influences and other disruptive factors. Play video Allow data transfer to/from vimeo.com? (learn more) Demonstrate: an autonomous aerial vehicle with a maximum weight of up to 25 kg that is able to complete a predefined course without any human intervention, even under the influence of inclement conditions. The aim is to develop a system that can master various challenging obstacles and tasks completely autonomously. Other autonomous systems, e.g. on the ground, can be used as support. The SPRIND Funke Fully Autonomous Flight started in February 2024. After completing the first stage in April 2024, the expert jury selected the participants for the second and final stage of the SPRIND Funke. Ten teams were able to qualify and, hence, get the chance to compete in front of industry experts and potential investors at the final drone race in September 2024. https://www.sprind.org/en/actions/challe.text: Funke complete Funke Tissue Engineering Topic Goal Teams FAQ Hello people with radical new ideas! We need pioneering solutions for the treatment of patients with artificial tissue. We need you. Many patients are dependent on donor tissue or organ donations. However, the high demand for donor tissue and organs cannot be met by far. Therefore, patients suffer from long waiting lists and countless medical challenges or die before a donation is available. Artificially produced tissue, on the other hand, promises a lasting improvement in the quality of life for these people. In recent decades, scientists, engineers and doctors have developed tools to construct biological substitutes that mimic natural tissue. However, the ultimate goal of overcoming the limitations of traditional organ transplantation remains unachieved. Demonstrate: the feasibility of a novel approach to tissue engineering for first-in-human transplantation. The aim was to develop an advanced concept that will produce the most refined artificial tissue to date. This tissue had be as close as possible to natural human tissue (size, structure, complexity) and may include elements such as the engineering of cells, the development of tissue architecture or engineered materials. Conclusion of the SPRIND Funke Tissue Engineering On November 1, 2023, the SPRIND Funke Tissue Engineering launched with four ambitious teams embarking a ten-month journey to explore and demonstrate the key characteristics of the artificial tissue. SPRIND provided up to EUR 500,000 in funding to support this groundbreaking work. Funke Tissue Engineering concluded after Stage 1 Stage 2, which would have included additional funding and support for planning first-in-human trials, did not take place. The milestones necessary to proceed to this stage were not fully met by a sufficient number of teams. Knowledge gained in Stage 1 provides crucial insights for future advancements in Tissue Engineering Innovation often involves discovering what works — and what doesn’t — before moving forward. Even when projects don’t continue along their envisioned trajectory, each phase offers learning opportunities that drive progress in the long term. SPRIND remains dedicated to fostering bold ideas and will continue to support innovators who push the boundaries of science and technology. https://www.sprind.org/en/actions/challe.text: Challenge complete Your Challenge: New Computing Concepts Topic Goal FAQ Contact Hello people with radical new ideas! We need breakthrough innovations to develop new, resource-saving computer concepts. We need bold ideas. We need you. In a digital world of the future, everyday life and the working world around us will be permanently supported by artificial intelligence. Data from countless sensors and actuators are read out by the smallest computers, processed, merged via a network of data links into larger nodes with more computing power, interpreted, fed back. They change, control, support, move our lives. In between sit huge data centers that take on the big tasks, manage and direct data, train artificial brains and solve complex scientific problems. But this vision of a connected world currently comes at a high price. If global energy consumption for computing and communications increases at the same rate as it has been, it will take up the entire, global capacity for energy production as early as 2040. Energy consumption has been falling for a long time - because chip structures have become smaller and smaller. But this is where developments are now reaching their physical limits. In order to implement our visions for the future - from autonomous driving to computer-aided drug development to intelligent control of countless renewable energy sources - fundamentally new computing concepts must therefore be found. Play video Allow data transfer to/from vimeo.com? (learn more) The challenge: to develop computing approaches that promise a significant reduction in resource consumption in terms of energy, time or space, or to address issues that have not been solvable to date. The goal of the Challenge was to develop fundamentally new computing concepts in theory and gradually transfer them into practice. The approaches must achieve high leverage in application. Either a specific problem with a high occurrence in application should be solved, for example the solution of partial differential equations, or a specific problem whose solution promises a significant gain in knowledge. Likewise, a generalist approach can be developed. We support: Breakthrough innovations It is clear to us: Teams participating in this Challenge are fully challenged. We at SPRIND therefore provide intensive and individual support. The challenge started in November 2022. In the first stage, the teams were funded with up to €250,000 over nine months and received additional funding as the challenge proceeded. The challenge was completed in July 2023. Our central concern as SPRIND is to bring ideas with the potential for a breakthrough innovation to market for the benefit of all of us. That is why SPRIND continues to support projects with disruptive innovation potential even after the Challenge has ended. OVERCOMING THE FLASCHENHALS In order to realize our visions for the future, we need entirely new computing concepts. In a comic essay, Dr. Julia Schneider and Noëlle Kröger address this need. https://www.ghst.de/silvia-tennenbaum-st.text: Silvia-Tennenbaum-Stipendium Writer-in-Residence-Programm Die weltweite Zunahme von antisemitischem Denken und Handeln ist eine zentrale Herausforderung für die liberale Demokratie. Mit dem Silvia-Tennenbaum-Stipendium gibt die Hertie-Stiftung Autorinnen, Kritikern und Künstlerinnen, die sich mit dem Themenkomplex Antisemitismus, Erinnerungskultur und Demokratie beschäftigen, die Möglichkeit, ein neues Projekt umzusetzen. Die Stipendiaten halten sich einen Teil der Zeit in Frankfurt auf und nehmen an internen und öffentlichen Veranstaltungen der Stiftung teil. Auf einen Blick Stipendiaten 2027 Das Stipendium Die Jury Kontakt Alexander Estis Der Schriftsteller Alexander Estis wird das Stipendium nutzen, um sich in einem literarischen Langessay mit aktuellen Phänomenen des Antisemitismus zu beschäftigen. „Die Bewerbung von Alexander Estis hat die Jury durch ihre außergewöhnliche Verbindung von literarischer Gestaltungskraft, analytischer Schärfe und gesellschaftlicher Relevanz überzeugt. Mit seinem geplanten Essayprojekt wird er einen wichtigen Teil zur hochaktuellen Debatte über neue Erscheinungsformen des Antisemitismus beitragen.“ Prof. Dr. Sascha Spoun, Mitglied der Jury Drei Fragen an Alexander Estis Sie beschäftigen sich mit Erscheinungsformen des Antisemitismus seit dem 7. Oktober 2023, insbesondere in Kultur und Medien. Was kommt in der Debatte in Ihren Augen derzeit zu kurz? Es fehlt an einem Verständnis der so überaus zahlreichen Erscheinungsformen des Antisemitismus, seiner staunenswerten Wandelbarkeit – bei einem ebenso staunenswert konstanten Kern. Der Antisemitismus ist chamäleonisch, chimärisch, aalglatt entgleitend, selbstverleugnend: Er umfasst oftmals seine eigene, sich selbst legitimierende Antisemitismusdefinition. Und er häutet sich immerfort. Seit dem 7. Oktober 2023 hat er wieder neue Erscheinungsformen entwickelt. Und jedes Mal glauben Menschen: Diesmal ist es anders, diesmal ist es kein Vorurteil, diesmal ist etwas Wahres dran, diesmal haben es die Juden doch nun wirklich zu weit getrieben. In einem Langessay wollen Sie Analyse, persönliche Erfahrung und Satire miteinander verbinden. Warum ist gerade diese vielstimmige literarische Herangehensweise für das Thema wichtig? Einerseits ist das vielleicht einfach mein Zugang zu fast allen Phänomenen. Andererseits sorgt vielleicht gerade die besagte Vielgestaltigkeit und Wandelbarkeit des Antisemitismus dafür, dass er rein definitorisch und analytisch, dass er von nur einer Seite, aus einer Perspektive schwer zu greifen ist. Die Literatur kennt Mittel und Wege, der Diffusität des Emotionalen Ausdruck zu verleihen. Und die Satire kann die daraus erwachsende Abstrusität und Monstrosität bloßstellen. Das Klischee wird im Lachen erschüttert. Der Antisemit, besonders der verschwörungstheoretische Typus, hält sich für wahnsinnig ernst, seine Anliegen für moralisch erhaben, dringlich und absolut; nichts trifft den Antisemitismus so sehr wie der Witz. Über welche Leserschaft würden Sie sich für das Buch freuen? Über eine Leserschaft, die bereit ist, zuerst zu lachen – und sich dann sofort zu fragen, warum ihr das Lachen im Hals steckenbleibt. Yari Or Yari Or ist Professorin an der Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences. Als Tochter eines Holocaust-Überlebenden beschäftigte sie sich für ein Dokumentarfilmprojekt intensiv mit dem Fall Oskar Gröning. Ihre Erfahrungen während dieser Recherche verarbeitet sie nun in einem Roman. „Yari Or setzt sich am Beispiel Oskar Grönings, des ‚Buchhalters‘ von Auschwitz, mit Ambivalenzen und Paradoxien im Zusammenhang von Geschichte und Erinnerungskultur auseinander. In einem literarischen Memoir reflektiert sie darüber, wie ein Dokumentarfilm, der Ordnung schaffen sollte, sich gegen seine Urheberin kehrt. Die obsessive Beschäftigung mit dem Täter von einst führt die Filmemacherin in die eigene Familiengeschichte, lässt vertraute Kategorien wie Täter und Opfer, Schuld und Unschuld brüchig werden und wirft schließlich die Frage auf, was Gerechtigkeit eigentlich sein kann.“ Prof. Dr. Maximilian Benz, Mitglied der Jury Drei Fragen an Yari Or Sie sind Tochter eines NS-Verfolgten und haben den Prozess gegen Oskar Gröning, den sogenannten Buchhalter von Auschwitz, filmisch begleitet. https://www.efre.nrw/einfach-machen/foer.text: Boost4Impact.NRW Nordrhein-Westfalen Kleine und mittlere Unternehmen Junge Gemeinwohlunternehmen leisten einen wichtigen Beitrag zur nachhaltigen Entwicklung von Wirtschaft, Umwelt und Gesellschaft. Die Förderung „Boost4Impact.NRW“ unterstützt sie in der kritischen Phase nach der Neugründung. Junge innovative Unternehmen mit einem gemeinwohlorientierten Geschäftsmodell – sogenannte Gemeinwohlunternehmen – nehmen eine wichtige Rolle bei der Bewältigung nachhaltiger, umweltorientierter und gesellschaftlicher Herausforderungen ein. Durch die Verbindung wirtschaftlich tragfähiger unternehmerischer Ansätze mit gesellschaftlichen Anliegen entstehen soziale und ökologische Innovationen. Junge Unternehmen sind wichtige Impulsgeber für den Einsatz technologischer Lösungsansätze für soziale Ziele und die Entwicklung von Geschäftsmodellen zum Klima- und Umweltschutz oder zur Ressourceneffizienz. Damit leisten sie einen wichtigen Beitrag zur nachhaltigen Entwicklung von Wirtschaft, Umwelt und Gesellschaft. Mit dem Förderaufruf „Boost4Impact.NRW“ sollen Jungunternehmen, die gemeinwohlorientierte Ziele verfolgen, bei der Marktfestigung verstärkt unterstützt werden. Denn junge Gemeinwohlunternehmen unterscheiden sich von konventionellen, primär gewinnorientierten Gründungsformen etwa im Hinblick auf Leistungsempfänger, Marktorientierung oder Rechtsformen und stehen vor besonderen Herausforderungen im Gründungsprozess und darüber hinaus. Einschlägige Studien deuten etwa auf einen höheren Unterstützungsbedarf sowie Hemmnisse bei der Kapitalakquise hin. Unterstützung bei der Kapitalsuche und Marktfestigung Neugegründete beziehungsweise junge Kleinstunternehmen mit einem gemeinwohlorientierten Geschäftsmodell sollen in der kritischen Phase der Kapitalsuche, der Akquise von Geschäftspartnerinnen und -partnern sowie insgesamt in der Phase der Festigung am Markt Hilfestellung durch dieses Programmangebot und konkret durch die folgenden Fördergegenstände erhalten. Zur Unterstützung bei der Marktfestigung sollen dafür notwendige projektbezogene Ausgaben zur Beauftragung von Dienstleistungen durch externe Dritte gefördert werden: Investitionen in materielle und immaterielle Wirtschaftsgüter und begleitende Coachingleistungen, die für die Entwicklung und Einführung gemeinwohlorientierter Produkte, Dienstleistungen und Fertigungsverfahren erforderlich sind. Förderbekanntmachung Boost4Impact.NRW Dokument herunterladen Häufige Fragen zu dieser Maßnahme Wer ist antragsberechtigt? Antragsberechtigt sind nicht-börsennotierte Kleinstunternehmen mit Sitz oder einer Betriebsstätte in Nordrhein-Westfalen, deren Gründung höchstens drei Jahre zurückliegt und die folgenden Kriterien erfüllen: Das Kleinstunternehmen erfüllt die Kriterien der Social-Business-Initiative und die KMU-Definition der Europäischen Kommission. Das Kleinstunternehmen hat noch keine Gewinne ausgeschüttet bzw. bei ihm wurden noch keine Gewinne entnommen. Das Kleinstunternehmen hat nicht die Tätigkeit eines anderen Unternehmens übernommen. Das Kleinstunternehmen hat kein anderes Unternehmen übernommen bzw. ist nicht aus einem Zusammenschluss hervorgegangen. Was sind die Einreichungsfristen? Eine Antragstellung ist vorbehaltlich der zur Verfügung stehenden Haushaltsmittel zunächst bis zum 31. März 2027 möglich. Nutzen Sie im Vorfeld bitte das Beratungsangebot. https://www.sprind.org/en/actions/challe.text: Apply now Your Challenge: ENGINEERING MICROBIAL CONSORTIA Topic Goal Participate Webinar FAQ Contact Hello, innovators! We need breakthrough innovations to orchestrate microbial communities with AI and shift chemical manufacturing beyond fossil fuels. We need circular biomanufacturing platforms and the mastery to control living complexity. We need you. UNLOCKING ROBUST BIOMANUFACTURING WITH AI AND MICROBIAL COMMUNITIES Most industrial chemicals and materials remain dependent on petrochemical feedstocks, locking modern manufacturing into non-renewable resources and high-volume greenhouse gas emissions. Biomanufacturing offers a sustainable path forward, but current approaches have hit a ceiling. Single-strain monocultures largely depend on highly refined, uniform feedstocks that cannot be supplied in sufficient volume to replace petrochemical production at scale. Nature solves this through multi-species microbial communities — consortia capable of digesting crude, variable feedstocks and executing multi-step chemical syntheses beyond the reach of isolated strains. So far, leveraging complex consortia meant inviting unpredictability and control failures that bioengineering couldn't solve. THE OPPORTUNITY: Emerging AI models, real-time sensing, and high-throughput automation are enabling engineering pathways previously thought impossible. By coupling predictive modelling directly to active bioprocess control, we can turn wild cellular teams into observable, controllable precision factories — accessing low-cost, minimally refined feedstocks at industrial scale. This SPRIND Challenge is funded by the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN) through its digitalisation initiative to close material cycles, part of the action programme implementing Germany’s National Circular Economy Strategy (NCES) . Play video Allow data transfer to/from vimeo.com? (learn more) The Challenge: Developing robust biomanufacturing processes with Microbial Consortia and AI The goal of this Challenge is to develop new kinds of robust, circular, end-to-end biomanufacturing processes for sustainable chemicals and materials using fermentation with microbial consortia. These processes will be continuously optimized and actively controlled through AI-supported Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) cycles. As these processes mature, they could turn waste streams and future feedstocks made from captured CO₂ into useful chemicals and materials, improving resource efficiency and helping close material and carbon cycles. Robust processes must deliver consistent, reliable production even as feedstocks vary, operating conditions shift, or chemical transformations generate toxic intermediates. We are calling for fully integrated manufacturing systems that unite feedstock preparation, biological conversion, active process control, product recovery, and formulation where needed. Teams will use AI/ML models to make quantitative predictions and enable closed-loop process control. We support: Potential breakthrough innovations The Challenge spans up to 38 months across three competitive stages. A jury of internationally recognized experts supports SPRIND in evaluating and selecting participating teams. With funding from BMUKN, SPRIND provides direct financial backing through individual fixed-price contracts based on team cost estimates, offering up to €4,300,000 per team across all three stages. In Stage 1 (14 months) up to €1,200,000 per team, in Stage 2 (12 months) up to €1,300,000 per team and in Stage 3 (12 months) up to €1,800,000 per team. To ensure teams reach their full potential, SPRIND also provides fully funded Shared Services (including consortium preservation, quality control, data development, and independent robustness evaluations) that are not charged against team funding caps. Throughout the Challenge, SPRIND offers operational coaching, access to collaboration partners, and matchmaking sessions with investors and industrial off-takers. The Competition Detailed information can be found in the call for submission and the participation agreement. Call for Submissions & Participation Agreement Participate The application period runs until November 16, 2026, at 11:00 (CET). All applications submitted by this deadline will be considered. https://www.sprind.org/en/actions/challe.text: Apply now Your Challenge: Measuring with Entanglement Topic Goal Participate Webinar FAQ Contact Hello people with radical new ideas! We need breakthrough innovations to redefine the limits of today’s sensor technology. We need quantum sensing for a new era of measurement technology. We need bold ideas. We need you. How precisely can we measure the world? Many technological developments depend on reliably detecting the smallest changes: from navigation and medical imaging to quality control in industry, the range of applications is vast. Yet the accuracy of today’s sensors cannot be improved indefinitely. Classical sensing technology is subject to a fundamental physical limit known as the Standard Quantum Limit (SQL). Quantum sensing opens up the possibility of overcoming this limit. In particular, the use of entanglement and other non-classical quantum correlations can enable measurements that cannot be achieved with conventional methods. Such quantum sensors have already been demonstrated in the laboratory. The crucial step, however, is still missing: translating the quantum advantage into a robust, application-ready technology. Higher measurement accuracy alone does not make a market-ready product. A quantum sensor must also perform under real-world conditions – reliably, reproducibly, and with a relevant advantage over today’s available solutions. Size, robustness, stability, cost, and energy consumption can be just as decisive as measurement accuracy. This is exactly where the Measuring with Entanglement Challenge comes in. Play video Allow data transfer to/from vimeo.com? (learn more) The challenge: Developing the next generation of quantum sensors that achieve demonstrable quantum advantages beyond the Standard Quantum Limit (SQL) or exploit genuine quantum correlations, and demonstrate a measurable advantage for specific applications and under real-world application conditions. The goal is to translate the technology from the laboratory into a concrete application. The quantum advantage should be made usable under real-world conditions and compared with solutions available today. We are looking for teams that push the boundaries of today’s sensing technologies and demonstrate what is possible with next-generation quantum sensing. We support: Potential breakthrough innovations The Challenge runs for a total of 25 months. Teams participating in this Challenge will be fully committed to the task. SPRIND therefore provides intensive and tailored support. This includes funding of up to €545,000 in Stage 1, up to €1,050,000 in Stage 2, and up to €1,680,000 in the final Stage 3 of the Challenge. In addition to financial support, SPRIND provides teams with individual advice, networking opportunities, and coaching. To enable teams to focus entirely on their innovations, funding is provided quickly and with minimal bureaucracy. Following a pre-selection, a jury will make the final decision on admission to the Challenge. Stage 1 will start on 23 November 2026 with up to 10 teams. The objective of this stage is to demonstrate the quantum advantage and define the application use case. After four months, the jury will decide, based on the interim evaluation, which up to eight teams will continue in the Challenge for a further eleven months and develop an application-optimised sensor design. At the end of Stage 2, another selection session will take place. Up to four teams will have the opportunity in Stage 3 to build prototypes over a further ten months and validate them in real-world use. The selection sessions generally take place in person at the SPRIND offices in Leipzig. In-person participation is mandatory. Teams should be incorporated by the start of Stage 1. Alternatively, they must credibly demonstrate their intention to establish a company and must be incorporated no later than the start of Stage 2. The Competition Detailed information can be found in the call for submission and the participation agreement. Call for Submissions & Participation Agreement Application The application period runs until November 9, 2026, at 12:00 (CET). All applications submitted by this deadline will be considered. https://www.eit.europa.eu/our-activities.text: The EIT Community New European Bauhaus invites eligible project partners from previous Connect NEB and Co-create NEB projects to apply for the Enhance NEB 2027 Open Call. Enhance NEB supports projects ready to build on previous results by strengthening what works, scaling their impact, or replicating successful approaches in new locations. The call will support four projects with up to €92 500 in EIT funding per project, over a maximum implementation period of 12 months. What selected projects receive Selected Enhance NEB projects receive support throughout their implementation period. In addition to funding, participating teams will have access to: Individual expert mentorship providing specialised support in design and business development An in-person meeting for Lead Partners at the end of the programme Potential additional online cohort sessions to exchange experiences, strengthen connections and support the development of partnerships Ongoing interaction with the EIT Community NEB team throughout implementation EU-wide visibility and communications support, including opportunities to showcase project results and success stories across EIT Community NEB channels and its wider European network Discover how to apply About this page Subject Audience Business Entrepreneurs Public Authorities Researchers Students Universities Tags opportunity

https://www.tagesschau.de/wissen/forschu.text: Interview Nobelpreisträger Hegemann "Ich bin natürlich überwältigt" Stand: 05.10.2026 • 21:37 Uhr Der Algenforscher Peter Hegemann hat Grund zum Feiern: Gemeinsam mit zwei weiteren Forschern erhält er den Medizin-Nobelpreis. In den tagesthemen berichtet er vom Nutzen der Optogenetik - und fordert mehr Mut von der Politik. tagesthemen: Vielleicht hatten Sie von diesem berühmten Anruf des Nobelkomitees ja zuvor schon mal geträumt - aber heute Morgen kam er dann tatsächlich. Und jetzt, ein paar Stunden später: Wie stark müssen Sie sich noch immer zwicken? Peter Hegemann: Ich bin natürlich überwältigt. Und man weiß am Anfang gar nicht, wie man damit umgehen muss. Und der Tag heute war ziemlich turbulent. Aber allmählich hat sich das bei mir etwas gesetzt. Und ich denke schon, dass es irgendwie real ist. Zur Person Peter Hegemann ist Hertie-Senior-Forschungsprofessor für Neurowissenschaften am Institut für Biologie der Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin. Gemeinsam mit dem Würzburger Biologie-Professor Georg Nagel und dem US-Forscher Karl Deisseroth erhält er den diesjährigen Nobelpreis für Medizin. Ausgezeichnet werden ihre Entdeckungen im Bereich lichtgesteuerter Ionenkanäle und Optogenetik. tagesthemen: Ihre Forschung, so das Nobelpreiskomitee, habe "unser Verständnis des Gehirns grundlegend verändert". Lässt sich das so zusammenfassen? Sie und die beiden anderen Nobelpreisträger haben ja buchstäblich Licht ins Dunkel des Gehirns gebracht. Hegemann: Ja, Licht ins Dunkel kann man in gewisser Weise sagen. Aber das gilt sicher für das Fliegengehirn, das man belichten kann, oder das Zebrafischgehirn. Beim Mausgehirn wird es schon schwieriger - und das menschliche Gehirn ist weitgehend dunkel. Wenn Sie da optogenetisch arbeiten wollen, müssen Sie einen Lichtleiter ins Gehirn reinstecken und dann können Sie ein kleines Volumen von ein bis fünf Quadratmillimetern belichten. Mehr nicht. Peter Hegemann, Medizin-Nobelpreisträger, zum Inhalt seiner Forschung tagesthemen, Das Erste, 05.10.2026 • 21:45 Uhr "Eine Technologie, die man sich lange gewünscht hat" tagesthemen: Und doch führt das dazu, dass man einen besseren Überblick schaffen kann, wo welche Bereiche wie funktionieren im Gehirn. Das ist doch im Prinzip das, wofür Sie ausgezeichnet wurden, oder? Hegemann: Ja, das ist natürlich eine Technologie, die man sich lange gewünscht hat, dass man einzelne Zellen in einem großen zellulären Verband aktivieren kann oder auch inaktivieren, um zu sehen, wofür sie gut sind und wofür nicht. Das heißt, funktionale Studien wurden durchgeführt, sodass man jetzt einzelne Zellen im Gehirn, im Hippocampus, Hypothalamus, präfrontalen Cortex besser menschlichen Funktionen zuordnen kann und weiß, was die bei Patienten tun und was sie vielleicht nicht tun. tagesthemen: Und das ist genau der Grund, weshalb sie heute ausgezeichnet wurden. Aber Stichwort Patienten: Wie berechtigt sind denn die Hoffnungen, die sich Patienten mit etwa Parkinson, Epilepsie oder Schizophrenie machen können, dass ihre Grundlagenforschung dann auch wirklich zu neuen Therapien führt? Hegemann: Ja, es ist immer die Wunschvorstellung der Politiker und der Journalisten, dass das gleich zu Therapien führt. Aber Sie wissen ja von anderen Krankheitsbildern, dass es Jahre oder Jahrzehnte dauert, bis man die richtig versteht. Und das Verständnis ist das, was durch diese Technik gefördert wird. Die Therapie ist noch mal eine andere Sache. Aber Sie haben dieses Werkzeug ja Forschenden zur Hand gegeben, die damit überhaupt erst Therapiemöglichkeiten ausloten können. Das ist der große Erfolg Ihrer Grundlagenforschung. Hegemann: Ich bin ja selber eigentlich kein Neurowissenschaftler, ich bin Algenforscher. Wir haben uns mit den Lichtreaktionen von Grünalgen beschäftigt und dabei einen lichtaktivierten Kanal entdeckt und charakterisiert, der einige Jahre später dann hauptsächlich durch Karl Deisseroth in die Neurowissenschaften eingebracht werden konnte. Also war das ein langjähriger Prozess und das hat eine Zeit gedauert, bis es sich als Werkzeug verbreitet hat - zuerst in den USA, leider Gottes, aber jetzt auch weitgehend in Deutschland und verschiedenen anderen europäischen Ländern. Und man ist dann schon im Nachhinein überrascht, wie eine Algenforschung letzten Endes zu einem präklinischen Forschungsfeld und möglicherweise auch zu einer Therapie führen kann. tagesthemen: ...und jetzt zu einem Nobelpreis. Inwieweit ist dieser Erfolg auch ein Erfolg für die deutsche Wissenschaft und den Forschungsstandort Deutschland insgesamt? https://www.ki.nrw/innovationswettbewerb.text: News-Eintrag · KI-Ökosystem Innovationswettbewerb »AIDEAS #1 – Ideen für zirkuläre Geschäftsmodelle« © Circular AI Hub 07.09.2026 Bundesumweltministerium sucht Ideen von KMU und Start-ups für die Circular Economy Wie kann KI die Kreislaufwirtschaft voranbringen? Unternehmen und Start-ups auch aus NRW sind aufgerufen, ihre Ideen bis zum 16. Oktober 2026 beim Innovationswettbewerb »AIDEAS #1– Ideen für zirkuläre Geschäftsmodelle« des Circular AI Hub des Bundesumweltministeriums einzureichen. Wie können Unternehmen von Geschäftsmodellen der Circular Economy profitieren? Und wie können Digitalisierung und Künstliche Intelligenz dabei zu einem echten Gamechanger werden? Der Circular AI Hub des Bundesumweltministeriums hat dazu den einstufigen Innovationswettbewerb „AIDEAS #1– Ideen für zirkuläre Geschäftsmodelle“ gestartet. Gesucht werden innovative Konzepte und neue Ideen, die KI zur Lösung zentraler Herausforderungen der Kreislaufwirtschaft einsetzen. Teilnehmen können Einzelpersonen, Unternehmen oder Teams aus Wirtschaft und Wissenschaft, bspw. Start-up-Teams oder akademische Spin-Offs. Eine interdisziplinäre Jury aus Wirtschaft, KI-Entwicklung und Politik wählt die zehn überzeugendsten Konzepte aus. Diese werden zur Weiterentwicklung finanziell unterstützt. Für den Wettbewerb stehen insgesamt 100 000 Euro zur Verfügung. Nach Abschluss des AIDEAS-Wettbewerbes sollen die vielversprechendsten Ansätze in den weiteren Innovationszyklus des Circular AI Hubs integriert und skaliert werden. Der Circular AI Hub des Bundesumweltministeriums unterstützt als Innovationsplattform Unternehmen und Start-ups darüber hinaus mit vielen weiteren Angeboten und Unterstützungsformaten. https://www.eit.europa.eu/our-activities.text: EIT Culture & Creativity has opened the New Ventures in Creative Tech (Spark) call, offering up to €30 000 per team alongside a nine-month venture-creation programme for early-stage founders. What does the programme offer? The first cohort focuses on tech-centric ventures in Materials & Built Environment, spanning fashion, architecture, and advanced and circular materials. The programme is aimed at founders who are already testing, building and validating a creative tech concept and are ready to turn it into a viable venture. Selected founders kick off with an in-person CreaTech Startup Sprint, a bootcamp hosted in a European city where they work on problem–solution fit alongside international experts, coaches and peer founders. This is followed by a nine-month online venture-creation journey, with coaching, mentoring and topic workshops led by international industry and business experts. Exclusive technology partnerships support venture development, while access to major European events provides visibility. Who can apply? The call is open to early-stage founders – individuals and small multidisciplinary teams – with an innovative business concept, no registered company and the ambition to build for-profit, scalable, tech-centric ventures within the CCSI. Applicants must be based in an EU Member State or a Horizon Europe associated country. Future programmes Future programmes will expand to additional sectors, with details to follow. How to apply Applications close on 16 November 2026 at 17:00 CET. Full eligibility criteria, timelines and application details are available here. https://kaw.wallenberg.org/en/calls/wall.text: Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation has established a long-term postdoctoral fellowship program at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. The purpose of the program is to bring outstanding young Swedish scientists to NTU for two years of postdoctoral research and studies. The program is open for all disciplines at NTU. The Postdoctoral Fellows are given the opportunity to participate in a broad range of interdisciplinary activities and programs that characterize NTU’s approach to research and education. After completing their postdoctoral visit, the Fellows will be supported upon their return to Sweden and use their experience from NTU for the benefit of Sweden. Hosts The applicant must contact the scientist in whose laboratory/department/institute at NTU the applicant seeks to work. The applicant is required to submit a well-thought-out research proposal with clear deliverables together with a support letter from previous supervisor(s) at Swedish universities as well as a detailed invitation letter from an NTU Faculty. Criteria and conditions Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation invites applicants for postdoctoral fellowships at NTU. At the time the postdoc period starts, the applicants should have a doctor's degree from a Swedish University no older than 2 years after the dissertation date as well as a connection to a Swedish University or corresponding non-profit research organization. Scientific merit, adjusted to the applicant's age, will be an important factor in the assessment. The applicant cannot be employed/Scholar at the intended host/University prior to the Wallenberg post-doc. The Stipend cannot be combined with other stipends or positions. The successful candidates will be employed by NTU with an annual base salary starting at Singapore dollar (SGD) 70,000. In addition, a family cost or cost of living allowance will be paid starting at SGD 30,000 and an annual research allowance of SGD 5,000 each year over their two-year fellowship. The Fellows will also receive the NTU standard health insurance. Following the postdoctoral studies there is an opportunity to receive funding from the Wallenberg Foundation to support a research position at a Swedish university for up to two years if the Fellow cannot find another position. After each year during the whole period a progress report shall be prepared and sent to the Foundation. After each year during the whole period a progress report shall be prepared and sent to the Foundation. A complete application should contain the applicant’s date of PhD dissertation, CV and include a list of publications, a short personal letter (max 1 A4 page or 3 500 characters incl. spaces) a brief description of the proposed research program and a description of the research profile of the intended host and supervisor (max 6 A4 pages, 21 000 characters incl. spaces). A letter of invitation from the intended host should be submitted with the application (Other appendices). If the applicant has not passed the doctorate exam at the time of the application, a letter from the supervising professor should be submitted, in which the actual date for the exam is stated (Other appendices). Each applicant should ensure that two separate letters of recommendation with comments on the research program are submitted with the e-application. Please note that a budget form is not required since the amount applied for is fixed. Submit instead a document, confirming if you intend to apply for the Accompanying family member allowance. The application shall be written in English. Application period The application period begins October 16. Last day of application November 16. E-application The Foundation uses an electronic application system. Please read the instructions for the e-application. Note that it is only allowed to submit an application within one of the Foundation’s postdoc calls. Go to E-application A list of successful applicants will be published on the website in late spring. Contact persons at NTU Professor Michael Khor Director, TRACS and Bibliometrics Analysis President’s Office Email: [email protected] Phone: (+65)65921816

The grant gives researchers the opportunity to develop their early-stage discoveries towards validated methods, products or processes and provides the opportunity to carry out activities that validate and accelerate the development of the project and prepare for innovation and commercialization. Proof of Concept in Life Science KAW in collaboration with SciLifeLab is opening a directed call for Life Science. The application period begins January 7, 2027. Last day of application February 5, 2027 at 1:00 pm. https://kaw.wallenberg.org/en/calls/knut.text: The Knut and Alice Wallenberg AI Consultancy Grant Calls strive to enable excellent scientific research, by ensuring that research groups with ongoing grants from Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, Marcus and Amalia Wallenberg Foundation and Marianne and Marcus Wallenberg Foundation get support to integrate AI in their research. Application period Application period begins November 20, 2026 Last day of application December 20 at 1:00 pm. Who can apply? One PI can apply maximum once every two years. Eligible to apply are scientists (PIs) that are employed at a Swedish University and have grants from theWallenberg Foundations under the following instruments: Wallenberg Academy Fellows Wallenberg Scholars Wallenberg Clinical Scholars PI and Co PIs in KAW projects Or are part of following KAW strategic initiatives: Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology (WACQT) Wallenberg Initiative Material Science for Sustainability (WISE) Wallenberg Wood Science Center (WWSC) Wallenberg Initiatives in Forest Research (WIFORCE) Wallenberg Centers for Molecular Medicine (WCMM) Data Driven Life Science (DDLS) SciLifeLab, including Fellows, group leaders, and infrastructure platform personnel Or have ongoing grants from Marianne and Marcus Wallenberg Foundation and Marcus and Amalia Wallenberg Foundation’s. Postdocs and PhD students cannot be the main applicant but could be an integral part of the proposed project. Application instructions (1 A4 page = 3500 characters including blanks). Project description (max 1,5 A4 pages) Please describe your research project. Make clear the i) background, ii) questions to investigate, iii) the added scientific value of integrating AI, iv) the expected timeline of the project. The project should start latest 31st of March. Available and planned data (max 1 A4 page) Please give a clear overview of the available and planned data to be used in terms of e.g. data types and volumes, number of samples, available labels, and other relevant information for the project. Also state the data provider or data repository, and when the data was/will be delivered or can be accessed. If applicable, include a schema of how the data is collected, stored, maintained and used in your current research. For logistic reasons, priority will be given to projects with at least some of the data already available for analysis, but AI4S experts can also assist with dataset generation for novel datasets. Applying research groups are assumed to be domain experts capable of working with and explaining data in their field, while AI4S experts provide insight into modelling, experimental design, and evaluation metrics. Involvement (max 1 A4 page) The research group must assign at least one scientist (at least at the level of PhD student) from the group to take part in the AI work to ensure efficient knowledge transfer and longevity of the project beyond the time of the granted support. It is a requirement that the scientist(s) can devote necessary time for this. It is advantageous, but not strictly required, that the scientist(s) assigned from the research group has some experience in working with data driven methods, such as statistics or some level of machine learning. Previous knowledge in AI is not a factor in the evaluation process. The application should include the CV(s) of the scientist(s) assigned to the project, as well as the CV of the PI. Compute availability Please indicate if your research group already has access to sufficient compute power. If you do not have access to such an environment or would like to get help in assessing whether the resources you have is sufficient, please indicate this in your application so that we can take this into account for project planning. Scope of grant Granted applications will be offered AI expertise by experienced AI specialists from AI4S AB for a maximum of 700 h effective time. Extensions and multiple project applications are on rare occasions possible, but the same research group (PI) can only be granted a maximum of 1000 h effective time over a period of two years. Only one application per principal investigator/group leader per four application rounds is allowed in these calls. Projects with previously granted support can apply for further assistance once. The exact amount of time granted will be decided on a case-by-case basis. The AI4S Consultant(s) will be fully integrated members of the research team during the time of their support, taking part in the scientific discussions and participating as co-authors of manuscripts according to normal contribution criteria. All work and analyses done will be fully available to the research group, including scripts and programs. Analysis tools and technical knowledge gained during the project will be made immediately public (i.e. directly after publication). The granted support is free of charge, as the cost is covered by Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation. Evaluation Process All applications are kept confidential through

https://kaw.wallenberg.org/en/calls/2028.text: The application period begins Januari 10, 2028. The Foundation supports projects with high scientific potential. Projects should be focused on a coherent research question where the complementary competencies of the participating scientists gives new possibilities to attack the chosen research question. Projects normally have a budget of between SEK 15 million and SEK 40 million. Projects can have a duration of three to five years. High-priority projects include new research areas and research that is interdisciplinary in nature. A project must have a freestanding purpose and not merely constitute auxiliary funding for current operations or other projects in progress. For subjects in which research is generic in nature, such as mathematics, a project can consist of joint concept development. Application period The application period for 2028 begins Januari 10. Last day of application February 4 at 1:00 pm. University Number of nominations Karolinska Institutet 15 Uppsala University 15 Lund University 15 Stockholm University 15 Chalmers University of Technology 10 KTH Royal Institute of Technology 10 University of Gothenburg 10 Umeå University 10 Linköping University 10 Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences 5 Luleå University of Technology 5 Others 2 Guidelines for research projects with high scientific potential Vice-chancellor’s letter of support According to Foundation rules, the vice-chancellor or the equivalent must approve the application. Co-investigators must spend at least 50 % of their position and working time in Sweden.
