https://kaw.wallenberg.org/en/calls/2028.text: Wallenberg Academy Fellows who received their grant in 2023 can be nominated for another five years of funding. Up to 60 % of the original Wallenberg Academy Fellows 2023 may obtain an extension. Swedish Universities and institutions of higher education are invited to nominate Wallenberg Academy Fellows appointed 2023 for the prolongation. Who can be nominated? Wallenberg Academy Fellows (WAF) who received their grant in 2023 can be nominated for another five years of funding. Up to 60% of the original Wallenberg Academy Fellows 2023 may obtain an extension. Swedish universities and institutions of higher education are invited to nominate Wallenberg Academy Fellows appointed 2023 for prolongation before February 7, 2028. The nominating University should guarantee that the researcher will obtain a relevant position at the University and is expected to take long term responsibility for their nominated Fellow. The following points need to be met for a nominated Fellow: The nominee should have received a Wallenberg Academy Fellows grant in 2023 (or 2021 or 2019 if the conditions in the last point stated here below is met) A researcher cannot simultaneously hold both a Swedish Research Council Consolidator Grant and a WAF prolongation grant. A Fellow cannot be nominated by more than one university for prolongation. The fellow must approve the nomination. Must spend at least 80 % of the position and working time at the host university. It is possible for a Wallenberg Academy Fellow 2023 to be nominated for a WAF prolongation, two years later (i.e. with WAF 2025) if the Fellow can, on request, prove documented parental leave, sick leave or defence service for more than six months during the project period. The financing of the Foundation for the WAF 2021 prolongation grant will include: A prolongation grant of SEK 2,200,000 will be granted per year during five years for all disciplines. Fellows who are not granted prolongation will receive a bridge grant of SEK 1 million for year 6 if the researcher maintains a relevant position at a Swedish university or an institution of higher education during this year. The universities co-fund the initiative by guaranteeing that 50% of the researcher’s salary is covered by the university. A university may choose to fund the researcher’s entire salary, thereby helping to give him or her a larger unencumbered research grant. The university will also co-fund the initiative by contributing to indirect costs and rent over and above the potential contribution from the foundation for indirect cost and rent. Up to 20% of the awarded amount can be used for indirect costs and rent. Documents Documents attached should all be English except for the popular scientific summary in Swedish. One A4 pages corresponds to 3500 characters including blanks. The nomination should include: Vice chancellor approval/ the University nomination – each nomination must contain a brief presentation of the reasons why the nominee´s activities are considered a key component of the research profile of the university and a description of the nomination process, i.e. the arguments, evaluations and processes on which the nomination was based (maximum two A4 pages) Project summary – a brief popular scientific summary in English, maximum 2000 characters including blanks A project proposal (maximum six A4 pages) The person’s research qualifications, i.e. CV (maximum two A4 pages) covering positions held, awards won and postdoctoral research stays, if any A short (maximum two A4 pages) account of the person’s career, i.e. primarily his or her academic achievements together with information of present support from universities or other financial support A list of all publications in peer-reviewed journals, with the ten most important publications marked. https://kaw.wallenberg.org/en/calls/2028.text: Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation together with Marianne and Marcus Wallenberg Foundation and Marcus and Amalia Wallenberg Foundation (Foundations) have set up a long-term program for young researchers: Wallenberg Academy Fellows. The program has been announced 10 times, and a total of 288 Fellows have been appointed. The Foundations have decided to announce the program in 2028, 2030, 2032 and 2034. In close cooperation with the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences, the Royal Swedish Academy of Agriculture and Forestry, the Royal Swedish Academy of Letters, History and Antiquities and the Swedish Academy, the Foundations have created a program that will provide resources for Sweden’s most promising researchers to develop their work. The program addresses young researchers in medicine, natural sciences, engineering and technology, humanities and social sciences. The purpose of the Wallenberg Academy Fellows program is to give young researchers working conditions that enable them to focus on research and tackle difficult, long-term research questions. The Swedish Academies will evaluate and select the most promising researchers, and the universities will then take long-term responsibility for these individuals. Swedish universities are invited to nominate candidates for the program. Application dates The application period starts on the 14th of August 2028. Universities are invited to nominate candidates to the program by 15 September 2028 at the latest 1 pm . Decisions will be announced in June the following year. Nominations for the program Each institution is allowed to nominate a maximum number of applicants as listed below: University Number of nominations Stockholm University 16 Karolinska Institutet 16 Uppsala University 16 Lund University 16 University of Gothenburg 12 Chalmers University of Technology 12 KTH Royal Institute of Technology 12 Linköping University 12 Umeå University 12 Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences 12 Luleå University of Technology 6 Others 4 The university should strive for 40 % of the nominations to be from the underrepresented sex. Only one internal candidate can be nominated for each international nomination (within the above maximum number of nominations per university). Who can be nominated? The program is open to researchers in all academic disciplines: medicine, engineering and technology, natural sciences, social sciences and humanities, and also in the interfaces between them. Candidates nominated in 2028 must have obtained their PhDs after 1 January 2019. An exception may be made for nominees whose PhD date back to before 2019 and who on request can document a leave of absence due to parental leave, military service or extended sick leave that has taken place since the PhD exam. A researcher cannot simultaneously hold a Wallenberg Academy Fellows grant and a recruitment package as part of the Foundation’s molecular medicine initiative (WCMM centra) or the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems Program (WASP), Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems Program - Humanities and Society (WASP-HS), Data Driven Life Science (DDLS), Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, (WACQT) Wallenberg Wood Science Center (WWSC), Wallenberg Initiative for Materials Science and Sustainability (WISE) or Wallenberg Initiatives in Forest Research (WIFORCE). The nominees must spend at least 80% of their position and working time at the host university. Nomination procedure A candidate cannot be nominated by more than one university. A candidate must, when nominated by a specific university, approve the nomination. Apply English Svenska English RJ Flexit RJ Flexit consists of grants for research and collaboration between researchers and other organisations in the private, public and non-profit sectors. RJ Flexit offers researchers, companies and other organisations within private, public and non-profit sectors the opportunities to collaborate, develop and exchange knowledge and experience. The purpose is to support collaboration between higher education and external parties. The researcher and company/organisation (host organisation) are to formulate a joint proposal for a research project. The project is to be based on a well-explained need of the host organisation that the researcher can address. The proposal also needs to have the support of the researcher’s higher education institution. RJ Flexit projects run between 1 and 3 years and are conducted at both the host organisation and the higher education institution. The researcher is expected to work for the mutual exchange of knowledge between the organisation and higher education institution throughout the project period and to actively participate in the network meetings organised through RJ Flexit. Apply English Svenska English RJ Infrastructure for Research With RJ Infrastructure for Research, RJ promotes future research in social sciences and humanities. The support is aimed at infrastructures of national or international significance that require larger investments than can be managed within the framework of individual research environments or research programs. The infrastructures that receive support should be in a development phase, and the technical solutions should already be proven and well-functioning. The research community's need and demand for the infrastructure should be well-documented at the time of application and already have a wider number of users. The grant does not cover research but only funds for the development and operation of infrastructures. Apply English Svenska English RJ Programmes RJ Programmes are joint, well-integrated research assignments in the social sciences and humanities carried out over relatively long periods by groups of merited researchers connected with Sweden. This means that it is a requirement that researchers active in Sweden participate in the research or that a Swedish research institute is actively involved. This also means that RJ allows the participation of foreign researchers based abroad. The researchers are free to define their own research tasks. Programmes require a highly developed research environment or researcher network, and advanced expertise on the part of the researchers and research leader. Research groups of this kind are characterised by being well established in the international research community, with considerable contributions, both national and international. The average size of RJ Programme grants to date has been approximately SEK 35 million, including LKP (employer's social-insurance contribution top-up) and indirect costs. RJ budgets for up to three programmes annually. This also means that RJ allows the participation of foreign researchers based abroad. The researchers are free to define their own research tasks. RJ Projects are approved for up to three years. Apply English Svenska English RJ Pro Futura RJ Pro Futura is a national cutting-edge research program in the humanities and social sciences where promising young researchers are given the opportunity to conduct research under very favorable conditions. RJ Pro Futura is part of RJ's strategic priority to strengthening capacity building in the humanities and social sciences. Researchers in RJ Pro Futura are given five years to conduct research and develop their skills, with one of those years spent at the Swedish Collegium for Advanced Study (SCAS) in Uppsala. Afterward, researchers may be offered tenure-track positions at the nominating university. Swedish higher education institutions authorized to award doctoral degrees in the humanities and social sciences can nominate candidates for the program. It is not possible to apply to RJ Pro Futura. Previous researchers in RJ Pro Futura now hold prominent positions in the Swedish university and research system. Apply English Svenska English RJ Research initiation RJ Research Initiation is intended to initiate activities that will in some way result in new research in the humanities and social sciences. This support form aims to facilitate initial scholarly processes and help define and delimit various scholarly questions for future research. In this way, it focuses on the phase of the research process in which research ideas are discussed and that precede the research. As such, RJ Research Initiation is intended to support arranging different types of scholarly meetings, such as conferences, seminars and workshops, and the creation of new research networks through scholarly meetings. RJ welcomes applications with international participation. Grants can vary in size, but their purpose is always to initiate new research by stimulating and promoting contacts in the research community. Apply English Svenska English RJ Sabbatical With RJ Sabbatical, researchers can receive funding to complete research already at an advanced stage and to write syntheses. With an RJ Sabbatical grant, senior lecturers and professors can spend six to twelve months completing research that is already at an advanced stage and write syntheses. Stays abroad are a part of RJ Sabbatical, thus promoting international ties for Swedish research and education. The grant is intended to enable grantees to conduct research to the full extent of their employment. The research period must be devoted to completing ongoing research projects that have reached an advanced stage or to writing major works or syntheses likely to be regarded as representing significant scholarship. Grants may be for applications that will result in monographs or in journal articles. Apply English Svenska English Advanced Studies Programme The Advanced Studies Programme is an international research initiative funded by Riksbankens Jubileumsfond (RJ), aimed at strengthening Swedish research in the humanities and social sciences through international collaboration. The programme offers researchers the opportunity to spend extended periods at one of four prestigious institutes for advanced study around the world. During their stay, researchers are given time and space to focus solely on their own work in a stimulating, interdisciplinary academic environment, free from teaching and administrative duties at their home institution. The aim is for researchers to build long-term academic networks and collaborations that benefit the Swedish research community — for example by organising seminars, conferences, or initiating joint research projects. The programme encourages both the deepening and broadening of the researcher's perspectives and fields of knowledge, as well as active participation in the academic context of the host institution. The following institutes are part of this collaboration: Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences at Stanford University (CASBS) https://casbs.stanford.edu/ L’Institut d’études avancées de Paris (IEA de Paris) https://www.paris-iea.fr The Stellenbosch Institute for Advanced Study (STIAS) https://stias.ac.za/ Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (WIKO) https://www.wiko-berlin.de/ Print 2025/04/07 Contact persons Dr Robert Hamrén Research Manager +46 8 506 264 07 robert.hamren@rj.se Dr Fredrik Lundmark Research Manager +46 8-506 264 21 fredrik.lundmark@rj.se

Apply English Svenska English Research on Research Ethics The call aims to strengthen Swedish research on ethical issues in research, particularly within the humanities and social sciences, though it is open to all academic fields. The initiative responds to an identified need for deeper knowledge about the principles, frameworks, and practices that shape the legitimacy and societal role of research. The goal is to encourage high-quality research that contributes both empirical insights and conceptual development in the field of research ethics. Relevant areas may include good research practice, peer review systems, publishing patterns, access to data, the function of researchers as experts, and the interpretation and application of ethical frameworks. The call invites projects that critically examine how ethical standards are formulated, understood, and applied in the research community. Research on Research Ethics is a joint funding initiative by the Royal Swedish Academy of Letters, History and Antiquities, Riksbankens Jubileumsfond, and the Swedish Research Council. The funders aim to foster critical reflection and knowledge development around the ethical foundations of contemporary and future research practices. Apply English Svenska English Future Challenges in the Nordics Future Challenges in the Nordics is a research programme supporting work in the humanities and social sciences that addresses major social and cultural challenges facing people in the Nordic countries during the 21st century. The programme seeks to promote research that deepens our understanding of the historical, cultural, social, and political processes that have led to the present, offering constructive perspectives on the path ahead. Humanities and social science researchers play a key role by critically examining how humans interact with their environment and institutions, contributing both knowledge and insight to ongoing societal development. The aim is to produce research that is accessible and useful for citizens and policymakers alike, supporting public dialogue and decision-making in the face of complex future challenges. The programme runs from 2021 to 2027. The programme is jointly funded by several Nordic foundations, including the Society of Swedish Literature in Finland, Riksbankens Jubileumsfond, the Finnish Cultural Foundation, the Swedish Cultural Foundation in Finland, the Brita Maria Renlund Memorial Foundation, and the Kamprad Family Foundation. Apply English Svenska English Mixed Methods: Innovative Method Development What happens when a research question is analyzed using a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods—both traditional and innovative—as well as a wide variety of empirical materials? And how does this work in practice? What becomes of issues like level of detail and comprehensive perspective? These are some of the questions addressed by the projects within RJ’s initiative Mixed Methods: Innovative Method Development in the humanities and social sciences. The background to this initiative lies in the development of digital technology and how research in the humanities and social sciences is therefore facing a range of new challenges and opportunities. The challenges for research are both methodological and related to the philosophy of science. The amount and accessibility of digital information is growing. Both the possibilities and limitations of current standard methods are being highlighted as new methods emerge for analyzing texts, images, and sounds more extensively, rapidly, and precisely. This shift also imposes new demands on technical competence, infrastructures for storage and accessibility, as well as on collaborations across disciplinary and national borders. As a result of this digital transformation, new combinations of qualitative and quantitative methods are being developed, along with a more holistic understanding of societal phenomena. Even traditional perspectives in the humanities and social sciences benefit from this methodological development. Apply English Svenska English Nordic Fellowship Programme The Nordic Fellowship Programme is a three-year initiative aimed at strengthening Nordic connections in the humanities and social sciences. As part of RJ’s strategic efforts to increase the internationalisation of Swedish research in the humanities and social sciences, a three-year Nordic fellowship programme – the Nordic Fellowship Programme – has now been established. Over the course of three years, Swedish researchers are offered a one-year placement at the Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies, the Centre for Advanced Study in Oslo, and the Helsinki Collegium for Advanced Studies. The researchers are given the opportunity to work in a dynamic and interdisciplinary environment, which often leads to new contacts and research projects. The institutes are also responsible for bringing each year’s fellows together to strengthen Nordic research networks within the framework of the initiative. Each fellow is admitted according to the criteria applied by the respective institute. https://www.bmftr.bund.de/SharedDocs/Bek.text: 30.09.2026 - 24.11.2026 Bekanntmachung Richtlinie zur Förderung von Projekten zur MINT-Studienorientierung und -begleitung (AkadeMINT), Bundesanzeiger vom 30.09.2026 Vom 23. September 2026 1 Förderziel, Zuwendungszweck, Rechtsgrundlage Der im Juni 2026 vom Bundesministerium für Bildung, Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend (BMBFSFJ) und vom Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) gemeinsam veröffentlichte Aktionsplan MINT+ erweitert die früheren Programme von 2019 und 2022 und legt den Schwerpunkt auf ein ganzheitliches, vernetztes Bildungsökosystem für den MINT-Bereich. MINT steht dabei nicht mehr nur für Mathematik, Informatik, Naturwissenschaften und Technik, sondern ist als interdisziplinäres, zukunftsorientiertes und -weisendes Lehr- und Lernfeld zu verstehen. Ziel ist es, MINT-Kompetenzen nicht nur als Fachwissen, sondern als Schlüsselqualifikation für kritisches Denken, kreative Problemlösung und gesellschaftliche Teilhabe zu etablieren. Der Aktionsplan fordert den Transfer wissenschaftlicher Erkenntnisse in die Praxis, die Skalierung erfolgreicher Bildungsansätze und die Integration von digitalen sowie zukunftsweisenden Themen wie Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) und Nachhaltigkeits­technologien in alle Bildungsstufen. Damit zahlt der Aktionsplan auch auf die Hightech Agenda der Bundesregierung ein und schafft die erforderlichen personellen, bildungs- und institutionellen Rahmenbedingungen, die für deren Realisierung nötig sind: Entlang von vier Handlungsfeldern schafft er eine qualitätsgesicherte Fachkräftebasis, stärkt die technologische Souveränität durch innovative Forschungs- und Transferstrukturen und sorgt dafür, dass digitale und KI-Kompetenzen chancengerecht und flächendeckend in der Bevölkerung verankert werden. Ergänzt wird der Aktionsplan MINT+ um eine crossmediale Kommunikationsoffensive, die über Testimonials und an niedrigschwelligen Kontaktpunkten Berührungsängste abbaut und eine positive MINT-Erzählung schafft. Der Fachkräftemangel in MINT-Berufen bleibt eine zentrale Herausforderung für unsere Wirtschaft und für die Sicherung unseres Wohlstands, insbesondere angesichts globaler Entwicklungen wie dem Klimawandel, der industriellen Transformation und der rasanten Digitalisierung. Ein zentraler Baustein des Aktionsplans MINT+ ist daher die Talent- und Fachkräfteförderung (Handlungsfeld 3). Hierfür sollen Nachwuchsförderprogramme, Forschungs- und Praktikumsnetzwerke sowie spezialisierte Studienpfade etabliert werden, um die technologische Souveränität zu sichern. Für den Bereich der MINT-bezogenen beruflichen Aus- und Weiterbildung gibt es bereits diverse Initiativen und Programme, um beispielsweise das Handwerk zu stärken sowie Berufseinsteigende und Professionals in Zusammenhang mit dem Strukturwandel arbeitsfähig zu machen beziehungsweise zu halten. Mit Blick auf die erforderliche Innova­tionskraft des Landes ist aber insbesondere die Fachkräftelücke bei den fehlenden Expertinnen und Experten, das heißt High Potentials und der wissenschaftliche Nachwuchs, in den Blick zu nehmen. Angebote zur Studienorientierung sowie zur kontinuierlichen Unterstützung für MINT-Fächer bestehen auch, sind aber bisher nicht ausreichend auf regionale Gegebenheiten, beispielsweise den anhaltenden Wegzug junger Menschen aus strukturschwachen Regionen in Ballungsgebiete, abgestimmt. An dieser Stelle setzt die Förderrichtlinie „AkadeMINT“ an: Ziel ist es, den Anteil von jungen Frauen in den MINT-Studiengängen zu steigern und Jugendliche und junge Erwachsene aus weiteren bisher in MINT-Studiengängen und bei Abschlüssen im MINT-Bereich unterrepräsentierten, schwer erreichbaren Zielgruppen („easy-to-ignore-groups“) zu erreichen. Mit der Förderung sollen MINT-Studiengänge prominent platziert und das Studienangebot für die Zielgruppen zugänglich und zudem dauerhaft attraktiv gestaltet, und so langfristig die Abbruchquote gesenkt werden. 1.1 Förderziel Das Förderziel der vorliegenden Bekanntmachung „AkadeMINT“ ist es, durch gezielte, nachhaltig angelegte Ansätze mehr junge Menschen zwischen 16 und 25 Jahren in ein MINT-Studium zu bringen und sie dort bis zum Studienabschluss zu halten. Zielgruppe sind Mädchen und junge Frauen sowie verschiedene schwer erreichbare Ziel­gruppen, sogenannte „easy-to-ignore-groups“. Dadurch soll erreicht werden, dass langfristig die Fachkräftelücke im MINT-Bereich verringert und die Innovationskraft des Landes durch ein diverseres Spektrum an Absolventinnen und Absolventen gesteigert wird. Ein Teilziel der Förderung ist die gezielte Erhöhung des Frauenanteils in allen MINT-Studiengängen, mit besonderem Blick auf bislang besonders männerdominierte Fachrichtungen, zum Beispiel Fahrzeugtechnik, Elektrotechnik und Informatik. Die Förderrichtlinie soll gezielt Projekte unterstützen, die die im Aktionsplan MINT+ beschriebenen Prinzipien in den Blick nehmen und den Übergang von Schule sowie außerschulischer Bildung zu einem erfolgreichen MINT-Studium und/oder zum Studi

https://www.bmftr.bund.de/SharedDocs/Bek.text: 30.09.2026 Bekanntmachung Bekanntmachung zur Förderung von Projekten zur Erarbeitung „Nachhaltiger Lösungen für kritische Rohstoffe durch internationale Forschungspartnerschaften – COMPASS“, Bundesanzeiger vom 30.09.2026 Vom 4. September 2026 Vorbemerkung Diese nationale Rahmenbekanntmachung COMPASS (Navigating Sustainable Pathways for Critical Raw Materials (CRM). A Collaborative Programme for Advancing Sustainable Solutions for CRM through International Research Partnerships) dient der Förderung binationaler Verbundvorhaben, die Beiträge für eine resiliente und langfristige Bereitstellung von Rohstoffen leisten. 1 Förderziel, Zuwendungszweck, Rechtsgrundlage Die sichere, nachhaltige und resiliente Versorgung mit primären Rohstoffen ist eine zentrale Voraussetzung für die technologische Souveränität, Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und Innovationskraft Deutschlands und Europas. Für Zukunftstechnologien wie erneuerbare Energien, Elektromobilität und Digitalisierung sowie für zahlreiche sicherheits- und verteidigungsrelevante Anwendungen kommt der Verfügbarkeit kritischer Rohstoffe 1 eine Schlüsselrolle zu. Trotz ambitionierter Ziele für mehr Recycling und Kreislaufwirtschaft wird der steigende Bedarf hieran auf absehbare Zeit weiterhin überwiegend aus primären, im Bergbau gewonnenen Rohstoffen zu decken sein. Umso wichtiger sind neue Technologien und Verfahren, die eine möglichst umwelt- und klimafreundliche Erkundung, Gewinnung und Aufbereitung der Rohstoffe ermöglichen. Deutschland und Europa importieren den weit überwiegenden Teil ihres Bedarfs an kritischen Rohstoffen. Die neuen Technologien und Verfahren sollen daher in internationaler Zusammenarbeit ent­wickelt und implementiert werden. Mit der vorliegenden Rahmenbekanntmachung leistet das Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) einen Beitrag zur Umsetzung der Hightech-Agenda Deutschland (HTAD). Der Fokus liegt auf der Siche­rung einer resilienten Rohstoffversorgung. Förderziel ist es, durch FuEuI 2 -Zusammenarbeit mit Partnerländern die Widerstandsfähigkeit von Rohstoffversorgungssystemen zu stärken, Abhängigkeiten zu reduzieren und Grundlagen für eine umweltfreundlichere und nachhaltige Primärrohstoffgewinnung und -aufbereitung zu schaffen. Gleichzeitig wird der Wissens- und Technologietransfer zwischen allen Innovationsakteuren beschleunigt, die Fachkräftebasis und Talente im In- und Ausland gestärkt und die europäische und internationale Zusammenarbeit in Forschung und Innovation ausgebaut. Um die Rohstoffversorgung in der Europäischen Union (EU) und in Deutschland langfristig abzusichern, hat die Europäische Union 2024 den Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA) 3 verabschiedet. Darin gibt sie sich Zielvorgaben für die gesamte Wertschöpfungskette strategischer Rohstoffe sowie deren Diversifizierung. So sollen unter anderem nicht mehr als 65 Prozent der in die EU importierten Rohstoffe aus einem einzigen Land bezogen werden. Dadurch sollen Abhängigkeiten verringert und die Versorgungssicherheit erhöht werden. Zur Flankierung dessen schließt die EU strategische Rohstoffpartnerschaften mit herausgehobenen Partnerländern weltweit ab. 4 Die Bundesregierung verfolgt ebenfalls eine gezielte Rohstoffpolitik und arbeitet mit strategischen Partnerländern weltweit zusammen. 5 Deutschland ist sowohl auf europäischer als auch auf internationaler Ebene hervorragend vernetzt und verfügt über langjährige wissenschaftliche, wirtschaftliche und politische Kooperationen im Rohstoffsektor. 6 Diese bestehenden Netzwerke bilden eine fundierte Grundlage, um gemeinsam mit Partnerländern, europäischen Institutionen sowie multilateralen Organisationen und national sowie international agierenden Unternehmen nachhaltige Lösungen entlang der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette primärer Rohstoffe zu entwickeln – von der Exploration, über die Gewinnung und die Aufbereitung. Ziel dieser Rahmenbekanntmachung ist es, diese Netzwerke und Kooperationen gezielt durch die Zusammenarbeit mit Partnerländern auszubauen und zu vertiefen. Im Fokus stehen dabei der Aufbau und die Stärkung europäischer und internationaler Kooperationen, der Wissens- und Technologietransfer zwischen Forschung, Industrie und staatlichen Akteuren sowie die Entwicklung gemeinsamer technologischer und strategischer Ansätze zur verantwortungsvollen Erkundung und zum umwelt- und klimafreundlichen Abbau und Aufbereitung primärer Rohstoffe. Durch die Förderung international ausgerichteter Forschungs- und Innovationsvorhaben sollen Synergien genutzt, gemeinsame Technologien, Verfahren und Standards entwickelt und die Grundlage für langfristige, vertrauensbasierte Partnerschaften geschaffen werden. Damit unterstützt die Bekanntmachung zentrale europäische (zum Beispiel CRMA) und nationale Ziele, auch im Hinblick auf eine Diversifizierung und Ausweitung der internationalen Zusammenarbeit im Rohstoffsektor. https://cascadefunding.eu/open-call-anal.text: Up to €50,000 for European SMEs FIERCE opens its second financing round to help European SMEs turn downstream space data into greener business practices, offering up to €50,000 per beneficiary from a total budget of €694,520 to contract External Service Providers on circularity, raw materials and environmental monitoring projects. About FIERCE FIERCE ’s mission is to accelerate the adoption of downstream space data and services (Earth Observation, remote sensing, satellite navigation) by SMEs, start-ups and scale-ups to drive Europe’s green and digital transition. Over its lifetime, the project aims to mobilise €2.5 million in financial support for 70 SMEs, provide specialised technical and business advisory (including up to 50 hours of mentoring) to 140 SMEs, enable over 15 innovation intermediaries to run local entrepreneurship initiatives, and build the FIERCE Learning Hub, a reference point of 50+ sector-specific learning resources and tools. The project also feeds its experience into policy recommendations for stronger SME support ecosystems. FIERCE About FIERCE 2nd Open Call This Open Call funds SMEs that want to contract External Service Providers (ESPs) to design, upscale or commercialise space-enabled green solutions or to adopt commercially available ones. Applicants fall into one of two project orientations: Type A – Internal Transformation: improving the applicant’s own processes to reduce resources, waste or pollution. Type B – External Transformation Project: creating or improving products and services for better resource management or environmental monitoring for the applicant’s users. Applicants must demonstrate potential to leverage downstream space data, and the call places particular focus on solutions addressing improvement of circularity, resource use and waste management; safe, resource-efficient and environmentally friendly management of primary, secondary and critical raw materials; and improved environmental monitoring. Why apply to FIERCE 2nd Open Call The call distributes a total budget of €694,520 , with each selected beneficiary eligible for up to €50,000 to implement their project, based on the budget declared in the application form and paid out only after successful completion and verification against an approved Transformation Plan. Funding is structured around three project types , each with its own voucher ceiling: Ideation projects: up to €25,000 for research-focused activities on new or immature ideas. Scale-Up projects: up to €50,000 for testing and validating proven concepts. Commercialisation projects: up to €25,000 for the final steps toward solution validation. Because the overall cap per beneficiary is €50,000, applicants requesting an Ideation or Commercialisation voucher (up to €25,000 each) can apply for two separate, clearly distinct projects, provided the first is successfully completed (Milestone Review passed) before the second begins, and both finish within the programme’s duration. Beneficiaries already supported under FIERCE’s First Open Call for Financing can also apply here, as long as their combined support stays within the €50,000 ceiling. 100% of the voucher value goes to the External Service Provider(s) , no additional costs are reimbursed. Who can apply? Eligible applicants are single entities registered, at the time of the deadline, in an EU Member State (including its Overseas Countries and Territories) or a Horizon Europe Associated Country, including Switzerland. They must fall into one of the following categories: Self-employed individuals (sole traders). Micro enterprises: fewer than 10 employees, turnover or balance sheet under €2 million. Small enterprises: fewer than 50 employees, turnover or balance sheet under €10 million. Medium-sized enterprises: fewer than 250 employees, turnover under €50 million or balance sheet under €43 million. This includes start-ups and scale-ups. How to apply to FIERCE 2nd Open Call Applications must be submitted in English through the online form . Each application must describe the proposed solution and the ESP service(s) required, including a price quotation from the intended ESP , either drawn from the FIERCE ESP Pool or an external provider proposed by the applicant, chosen to reflect market value and the Best Value for Money principle. Applicants can submit up to two proposals, may modify a submission until the deadline, and only the latest version of each application is carried forward to evaluation. Results notification and onboarding: by January 2027. Programme start: February 2027, once the Sub-grant Agreement (SGA) is signed. https://cascadefunding.eu/fortis-open-ca.text: Up to €250,000 to deploy and scale human-centric robotics Solutions FORTIS Open Call #2 offers up to €250,000 per project to organisations that can deploy, integrate, or scale human-robot interaction (HRI) technologies either within FORTIS’s own industrial pilots or in entirely new civilian sectors such as agriculture, healthcare, or airports. About FORTIS FORTIS is an initiative developing solutions that help and support humans at work by augmenting the workforce while keeping people firmly in the loop. The consortium’s approach to human-robot interaction (HRI) is holistic: it works on enabling robots to interact with human workers in a natural, human-like way over long periods, combining both physical and non-physical communication channels. FORTIS pursues four main objectives: developing a human-centric solution for modelling and analysing humans; developing a flexible, agile multi-robotic solution that interacts with humans; integrating a safe and trustworthy HRI solution that optimises operations for both humans and robots; and demonstrating all of this through pilots in construction, railways, and manufacturing. The project’s tangible expected outcomes span three areas of impact: human-centric (better modelling of human behaviour and more intuitive collaborative robots); robot-centric (new testing and experimentation capabilities for HRI scenarios); and trustworthy interaction (improved efficiency, safety, and reduced need for costly physical prototyping). FORTIS About FORTIS Open Call #2 This second Open Call expands the deployment and reach of FORTIS technologies through two topics: Topic OC#2.1 – Pushing towards the deployment of FORTIS. This topic engages industry, research, and societal players to integrate third-party systems into the FORTIS framework , adapting and extending existing FORTIS toolkits for real-world deployment within the project’s own pilot environments. It is organised into 8 technical subtopics, grouped into three areas: Human-robot collaboration: Optimisation of HRC/task allocation; Flexible Interface Digital Twin; HRI Watchdog (assessing ethical, safety, privacy, cybersecurity and regulatory risks, including EU AI Act and Cyber Resilience Act compliance); HRI Activities Digital Twin; Omnideployment of the FORTIS solution (smart orchestration of AI modules across edge and server infrastructure). Human and AI perspectives: Ergonomics-Aware Human State and Interaction Context for Adaptive HRC; Interfaces with XR (AR/MR smart glasses as a bidirectional interaction layer between operators and robots). Robotics and AI perspectives: Trust-Aware Multi-Sensor Localisation and Mapping for FORTIS robotic platforms. Topic OC#2.2 – Exploiting the FORTIS solution in other key sectors. This is an open topic aimed at end-users and SMEs outside the current pilot domains. Applicants must identify a relevant civilian HRI use case and integrate two or more FORTIS ROS packages into their own solution, focusing on technology transfer and cross-sector adoption rather than new technology development. Priority sectors (at least 50% of this topic’s funding) are agriculture, mining, forestry, and fishing, with healthcare, events, airports, and shopping malls also eligible. Construction, manufacturing (material delivery/AGV logistics), and railway maintenance are explicitly excluded from this topic, since they overlap with FORTIS’s existing pilots. Why apply to FORTIS Open Call #2 The call has an indicative total budget of €3,142,746.92 , split as €2,065,373.46 for Topic OC#2.1 (up to €250,000 per project, for at least 8 projects) and €1,077,373.46 for Topic OC#2.2 (up to €170,000 per project, for at least 6 projects). Funding covers 100% of costs for non-profit organisations and 70% for SMEs and other for-profit entities and is paid as lump sums released at the end of each of three programme sprints. Beyond the funding, selected projects get dedicated administrative and technical mentoring and support in identifying exploitable assets and building a market-adoption roadmap. Who can apply? Eligible entities: research organisations/universities with a track record in the relevant sectors, and mid-caps, SMEs, or startups whose core business involves HRI technology development. Sectors of activity (for non-academic applicants) include computational/artificial intelligence, autonomous and intelligent robots, robot learning and programming, human-robot interaction, IoT, human factors, and biosignal processing. Topic OC#2.2 additionally opens participation to SMEs and end-users in agriculture, forestry, mining, fishing, healthcare, events, airports, and shopping malls. Consortium requirements: proposals must be submitted by a multidisciplinary consortium of 3 entities minimum for Topic OC#2.1 (multi-country, at least 2 different eligible countries) or 2 entities minimum for Topic OC#2.2 (single-country consortia allowed). https://cascadefunding.eu/futureprooftex.text: Up to €50,000 for European Textile SMEs FutureProofTextiles is opening its first call for proposals, offering €50,000 lump-sum grants to European textile SMEs pursuing either digital transformation or green transition projects, as part of a €2,000,000 cascade funding programme targeting 40 SMEs across the sector. About FutureProofTextile FutureProofTextiles : SME Support for Digital and Green Resilience mission is to help small and medium enterprises in the European textile sector overcome resource limitations and adopt advanced digital and sustainable technologies , boosting efficiency, reducing waste, and building a resilient cross-border innovation ecosystem. Ahead of launching its open calls, the consortium carried out a dedicated Needs Assessment survey of 150 stakeholder SMEs , and applicants are expected to explicitly demonstrate how their proposed innovation addresses the barriers and needs identified in that assessment: chiefly limited access to finance, digital and green skills gaps, uncertainty in selecting technologies, and unclear sustainability regulations. FutureProofTextile About FutureProofTextile Open Call 1 This first Open Call is designed to help SMEs navigate the “twin transitions” of digital transformation and green sustainability, distributing cascade grants across two parallel financing schemes: Green Initiatives: promoting sustainable practices and circular economy adoption, energy-efficient production, responsible textile waste disposal, and improved resource efficiency. Eligible activities are grouped into five categories: Circular Economy and Sustainable Manufacturing Activities Textile Waste Reduction and Resource Efficiency Activities Sustainable Materials and Green Production Activities Circular Business Models and Sustainable Market Uptake Activities CO₂ Reduction and Environmental Impact Activities Digital Innovations: adopting advanced digital tools, automation, and data-driven decision-making to improve efficiency and productivity. Eligible activities are grouped into three categories: Digital Transformation and Smart Manufacturing Activities Digital Product and Service Innovation Activities Digital Skills and Organisational Capacity Activities The call also pursues a regional inclusiveness target, aiming to support at least 4 SMEs established outside the core consortium partners’ regions. Why apply to FutureProofTextile Open Call Each selected SME receives a €50,000 lump-sum grant , part of a €1,000,000 total budget allocated for this call, split evenly between the two financing schemes: 10 SMEs per scheme. The grant requires a minimum €10,000 self-funding contribution from the beneficiary, bringing the total eligible project budget to €60,000. Funding is disbursed as a lump sum across three milestone-based tranches (40% / 40% / 20%), and projects run for a 9-month implementation period. Beyond the grant, beneficiaries gain access to tailored training, dedicated mentoring, and cross-border networking opportunities, detailed further below. Who can apply? Applicants must qualify as an SME under European Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC. Each application must represent a single SME, consortia of multiple SMEs, clusters, and intermediary organisations are not eligible , even if the latter qualify as SMEs. Applicants must operate in the textile value chain ; SMEs from complementary sectors (e.g., tech, machinery) are also eligible if their proposed innovation directly contributes to the textile value chain. Activities must align with one of the following NACE codes (or national equivalent): – Textile manufacturing: C13.1, C13.2, C13.3, C13.9 – Apparel manufacturing: C14.1, C14.3 – Textile-based products and technical textiles: C15.12, C22.19 – Textile recycling and circularity: C38 – Digital and innovative solutions for the textile sector: J62, J63 – Manufacture of machinery for textile, apparel and leather production: C28.94 Only SMEs legally established in Single Market Programme (SMP) participating countries (EU Member States and formally associated countries) are eligible. The applicant SME must have at least one staff member who speaks English and will be actively involved in implementation. Proposals must demonstrate a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 5 or higher. SMEs may submit up to two proposals per Open Call round (one Green Transition, one Digital Innovation) , but each SME can receive a maximum of one grant award across the entire programme. How to apply to FutureProofTextile Open Call Applications must be submitted exclusively online via the EU Survey application portal . Proposals must be written in English ; submissions in any other language will not be evaluated. A separate application is required for each financing scheme. The required documentation package includes the Standardized Application Form Template, the “Tables with Activities, Budget, Milestones and Risks” document, a signed SME and Eligibility Declaration form, and a signed Funding Eligibi

https://cascadefunding.eu/trunsport-open.text: Up to €60,000 for Transport-Sector Organisations TRUNSPORT’s first Open Call offers transport operators, infrastructure managers, technology providers, and public bodies across road, rail, air, and water up to €60,000 in lump sum grants to test and validate cybersecurity solutions against real transport-sector threats, with 21 grants available in this round. About TRUNSPORT TRUNSPORT is a European cybersecurity initiative that is building a next-generation Cyber Security Hub (CSH): a one-stop platform that maps and visualises transport and industrial systems so operators can understand connections, dependencies, and critical paths, and receive automated, tailored cybersecurity recommendations. The CSH is structured around three core service modules: Preparedness Support Services (PSS) for threat and risk assessment, continuous risk monitoring, and vulnerability testing; Human Shield Strategies (HSS) for training, awareness, and human-centric defence; and Mutual Assistance Support (MAS) for cross-organisation threat intelligence sharing and coordinated incident response. TRUNSPORT engages external organisations in validating this ecosystem precisely through two Open Calls. TRUNSPORT About TRUNSPORT Open Call 1 Open Call 1 targets organisations operating in the NIS2 transport sectors (road, rail, air, and water) inviting them to pilot, test, and validate cybersecurity tools, technologies, and methodologies in operational or representative environments. It is the first of two sequential rounds; a future Open Call 2 will extend the same opportunity to other OT/IT-based critical infrastructure sectors beyond transport. The call pursues five objectives: strengthening transport organisations’ cyber preparedness ; building cybersecurity awareness and readiness; supporting real-life experimentation and pilot validation ; stimulating collaboration ; and integrating new external entities into the TRUNSPORT ecosystem to help refine and validate the CSH itself. To ground these objectives, 41threat challenges across five transport domains have been established, proposals are expected to those: Air Transport (9) e.g. compromised boarding-pass or biometric validation systems manipulated baggage-handling controllers, or AI-generated deepfake social engineering against airport staff. Road Transport (15) e.g. manipulation of Variable Message Signs, traffic signal controllers, electronic tolling, or connected-vehicle (C-ITS) communications. Public and Multimodal Transport (4) e.g. tampering with smart ticketing systems, real-time passenger information displays, or false emergency alerts. Rail Transport (5) e.g. attacks on level-crossing systems, ERTMS train-to-trackside communications, or rail passenger information systems. Maritime and Inland Waterways (8) e.g. GPS/AIS spoofing of vessel navigation, compromised port terminal operating systems, or attacks on lock and bridge control systems. Why apply to TRUNSPORT Open Call 1 TRUNSPORT’s budget for Open Call 1 is of €1,260,000, spread across 21 grants. The maximum grant per project is up to €60,000 (lump sum scheme), covering a maximum of 50% of total project costs; so, applicants must co-finance at least the other half. Payments follow a three-tranche schedule tied to deliverables and project milestones: D1 – M1 (Description and Planning Report); D2 – M4 (Intermediate progress report) and D3 – M9 (Implementation and validation report. Beyond the money, selected beneficiaries gain direct access to the TRUNSPORT Cyber Security Hub, expert mentoring, and a structured 9-month support programme. Who can apply? Open Call 1 is open on equal terms to a broad range of entities operating in or serving the transport sectors , including: Transport systems operators, transport service providers, and infrastructure managers. Technology and digital providers, IT solutions providers and integrators. SMEs and startups, including those in the ITS (Intelligent Transportation Systems) space. Logistics and freight transportation companies. Consulting companies in the transportation and cybersecurity domains. Universities, research organisations, and NGOs. Related public sector entities, organisations, and authorities. Both single applicants and consortia may apply , and the €60,000 cap applies regardless of whether the applicant is one organisation or several partners jointly. How to apply to TRUNSPORT Open Call 1 Applications must be submitted exclusively through the F6S platform . All documents must be in English and submitted as PDF , following the official proposal template (Arial font, minimum 9pt, A4 page size, 15mm margins). A complete application includes the Application Form, Budget Template, Declaration of Honour, Ownership Control Declaration, and — where applicable — a Consortium Declaration and SME Declaration. Only the last submitted version of an application is evaluated if multiple versions are uploaded. Important dates Call opens: 30 July 2026. Deadline for clarification questions

https://www.eiturbanmobility.eu/call-for.text: Skip to content Home > EIT Regional Innovation Booster (EIT RIB) Hungary 2027 EIT Regional Innovation Booster (EIT RIB) Hungary 2027 15 September 2026 EIT Urban Mobility, with the support of the Hungarian National Innovation Agency (NIÜ), invites Hungarian start-ups to apply to the EIT Regional Innovation Booster (EIT RIB) Hungary 2027. This seven-month international market-access programme supports mature, innovation-driven Hungarian companies to validate, enter and grow in a new European market. A single cohort of eight companies will be selected and equipped with a validated market entry strategy, concrete connections in their target market, and the operational know-how to act on them. At the heart of the programme is a Buddy system that pairs each company with an experienced operator who already knows the chosen target market and sector. This is complemented by expert mentoring, a programme of workshops and guest speaker sessions, and a EUR 2.500 conference and travel grant to support in-person engagement in the target market. About the EIT RIB programme The programme runs from December 2026 to June 2027 and is structured in two consecutive phases. Phase 1: Market Preparation (Months 1–3) Selected companies validate their target market, assess their readiness for international expansion, and build an executable market entry strategy. Phase 2: Market Expansion (Months 4–7) Each company works up to 40 hours with its matched EIT RIB Buddy to start entering the chosen target market, supported by continued workshops and guest speakers, international matchmaking, and optional participation in EIT Community events. Benefits for participants 20 hours of 1:1 expert mentoring in Phase 1 40 hours of support from a matched EIT RIB Buddy with deep, hands-on expertise in the chosen European target market in Phase 2 A programme of go-to-market workshops and guest speaker sessions across the seven months A EUR 2,500 lump-sum travel and conference package to support in-person market entry International matchmaking and access to the wider EIT Community EIT funding allocation The total EIT funding allocated to this Call is EUR 20,000. Each of the eight selected companies receives a fixed lump-sum grant of EUR 2,500, provided as a travel and conference package to support market entry activities in Phase 2. Who can apply? The programme is designed for innovative, growth-oriented Hungarian start-ups that have already established a strong position in their domestic market and are ready to scale internationally. To be eligible, applicants must: Be a for-profit SME (according to the EU definition) registered in Hungary Have at least 3 full-time employees (FTEs) at the time of application Hold full ownership of, or exclusive commercialisation rights to, the intellectual property behind the solution to be taken abroad Have a novel product, service, technology or deep tech solution with demonstrated product-market fit in Hungary and proven commercial traction Operate in one of the EIT thematic areas: Climate, Digital, Food & Agritech, Healthcare, Energy and Renewables, Raw Materials, Urban Mobility, or Culture & Creativity. Full admissibility and eligibility conditions are set out in the Call Manual, Section 5.2 How can you apply? Applications are submitted through the EIT Urban Mobility Programmes Portal (NetSuite) . Before you begin, verify or register your organisation’s Participant Identification Code (PIC) on the EU Funding & Tender Opportunities Portal , then complete your registration in the Programmes Portal. The full step-by-step process is described in Section 7 of the Call Manual. Your application must include: The completed application form, in English A valid SME company registration certificate (PDF), confirming legal incorporation in Hungary A pitch video of up to 4 minutes Registration in NetSuite can take up to two working days, so please register well before the deadline to ensure a timely submission. https://www.eiturbanmobility.eu/call-for.text: Skip to content Home > Financial Support to Startups Open Call Financial Support to Startups Open Call 23 December 2025 Apply now This call is designed to strengthen Europe’s capacity to innovate and tackle pressing urban mobility challenges. By funding early-stage ventures , we aim to stimulate the growth of pre-seed, seed, and Series A companies , amplify the impact of EIT-funded research and innovation activities, and foster collaboration across industry, academia, cities, and startups. The initiative supports the development of high-impact solutions that reduce congestion, lower carbon emissions, improve safety and security, and enhance accessibility, while ensuring de-risked, high-quality investment opportunities aligned with the EIT Urban Mobility Financial Support thesis. EIT Urban Mobility will provide financial support of up to €2.5 million per company , for startups developing breakthrough mobility solutions . The purpose of this document is to invite eligible companies to apply for this financial support. Funding is provided through an open application process with multiple cut offs throughout 2026, 2027 and 2028: Cut-off 1: 23 February 2026 (17.00h CET) Cut-off 2: 18 May 2026 (17.00h CET) Cut-off 3: 31 August 2026 (17.00h CET) Cut-off 4: 16 November 2026 (17.00h CET) Cut-off 5: 11 January 2027 (17.00h CET) Cut-off 6: 12 April 2027 (17.00h CET) Cut-off 7: 30 August 2027 (17.00h CET) Cut-off 8: 15 November 2027 (17.00h CET) Cut-off 9: 10 January 2028 (17.00h CET) Cut-off 10: 13 March 2028 (17.00h CET) This Call for Applications is open to startups that are already engaged in an ongoing funding round . EIT Urban Mobility aims to participate in such rounds alongside venture capital or other private investors, fostering co-investment opportunities that strengthen the ventures’ financial position and growth trajectory. EIT Urban Mobility will not lead a funding round and, consequently, will not assume the role of lead investor, unless exceptional circumstances occur. To accelerate the transition to sustainable mobility in cities, this Call focuses on five sectors in which we believe Europe has the potential to innovate and create impact. Urban logistics, Public and shared transport, Mobility data management, Electrification & alternative fuels, and Health and mobility. In the future, this call may also include specific topic scopes to address key market opportunities or urgent market failures that can be addressed through our funding. EIT Urban Mobility is committed to fostering a more equitable, diverse and inclusive innovation ecosystem. Proposals with diverse teams and clear strategies for inclusive innovation will be positively assessed during the evaluation phase. Who can apply? This Call for Proposals is open to all legal entities established in the Member States of the European Union, and/or in Third countries associated with Horizon Europe . To be considered eligible for this Call, applicants must also meet all the following mandatory criteria. Applications that do not fulfil these criteria will not be considered eligible. https://www.eiturbanmobility.eu/call-for.text: Skip to content Home > Enhance NEB 2027 Open Call Enhance NEB 2027 Open Call 15 September 2026 EIT Urban Mobility, as lead of the EIT Community New European Bauhaus, invites eligible partners from previous Connect NEB and Co-create NEB projects to submit proposals to the Enhance NEB 2027 Open Call . Enhance NEB provides funding for previous Connect NEB and Co-create NEB project partners to strengthen, scale or replicate place-based solutions , building on the achievements of their previously funded projects. Through the Enhance NEB 2027 call, selected teams will have up to 12 months to consolidate their work, expand its impact or adapt successful approaches to new locations, while continuing to collaborate and co-create with communities and relevant stakeholders. Applications are open until 17 November 2026, 17.00 CET . About the New European Bauhaus and this call The New European Bauhaus is an EU initiative supporting the creation of places that are sustainable, inclusive and beautiful . The EIT Community New European Bauhaus , led by EIT Urban Mobility in collaboration with EIT Food and Climate KIC, supports local actors, initiatives, start-ups and public administrations to co-create and scale NEB-aligned solutions across Europe. Through the Enhance NEB Open Call 2027 , eligible previous Connect NEB and Co-create NEB project partners can take their work further through one or more of three pathways: Strengthening existing projects by deepening collaboration, consolidating successful approaches and increasing their long-term impact. Scaling up solutions by expanding partnerships, geographical reach, target groups and overall impact. Replicating successful approaches in new locations, adapting them to different local contexts and establishing the partnerships needed for implementation. All proposals must contribute to the three core New European Bauhaus values — Sustainable, Beautiful and Together — and align primarily with one of three thematic areas: Urban Mobility, Food or Climate . EIT funding allocation The total estimated EIT funding allocated to this Call is €370,000 , with four projects expected to be selected. Each project may receive up to €92,500 of EIT funding . Proposals must include a minimum co-funding contribution of 20% , as set out in the Call Manual. Projects may run for a maximum of 12 months , with implementation expected between March 2027 and February 2028. Who can apply? Enhance NEB is a multi-beneficiary call open to consortia of 2–4 legal entities , with at least two entities independent of each other. The Lead Partner must have participated , either as Lead Partner or consortium partner, in an eligible 2025 or 2026 Connect NEB or Co-create NEB project , as listed in Annex 4 of the Call Manual. The remaining consortium partners do not need to have participated in a previous Connect NEB or Co-create NEB project , meaning new organisations are welcome to join the proposal. Each consortium must include at least one city or other local or regional public authority, or an entity affiliated with one . Applicants must be established in eligible countries, as defined in the Call Manual. For full eligibility requirements and special cases, applicants should refer to the Call Manual. https://www.eiturbanmobility.eu/call-for.text: Skip to content Home > Strategic Innovation Open Call Strategic Innovation Open Call 19 June 2025 Apply now EIT Urban Mobility invites innovators from across Europe to submit a proposal to its Strategic Innovation Open Call, designed to accelerate the deployment of impactful solutions that address the most pressing challenges in urban mobility. The call focuses on supporting ambitious, market-critical projects that tackle clearly defined problems faced by cities, public authorities, and mobility providers. We aim to de-risk development and enable large-scale deployment by backing solutions with a clear path to market and the potential to scale across Europe. Through this call, EIT Urban Mobility fosters innovation and strengthens Europe’s competitiveness by encouraging collaboration across the EIT Knowledge Triangle—education, research, and business—alongside a fourth essential partner: cities. The Call will focus on five sectors in which we believe Europe has the potential to innovate and create impact: Urban logistics, Public and shared transport, Mobility data management, Electrification of transport and alternative fuels, and Health and mobility. In the future, the Call may also include specific topic scopes to address key market opportunities or urgent market failures that can be addressed through our funding. EIT funding allocation The total estimated funding allocated to this Call is 60 million EUR for the period 2026-2028 and has multiple cut-off dates. Each project may receive up to 2 million EUR of EIT funding. EIT Urban Mobility will reimburse up to 65% of the eligible project costs, while the minimum co-funding rate for all proposals is 35%. Who can apply? This is a multi-beneficiary call for proposals and therefore there must be a minimum of two independent legal entities, working together. These entities must be established in two different European Member States, and/or Third countries associated with Horizon Europe . For information on special cases, including Switzerland and Hungarian universities please refer to the Call Manual (see ‘List of documents to take into consideration’ section below) . https://www.eiturbanmobility.eu/call-for.text: Skip to content Home > Connect & Co-create NEB 2027 Open Call Connect & Co-create NEB 2027 Open Call 15 July 2026 EIT Urban Mobility, as lead of the EIT Community New European Bauhaus, invites organisations from across Europe to submit proposals to the Connect NEB & Co-create NEB 2027 Open Call , supporting local ideas and neighbourhood transformation inspired by the New European Bauhaus. The call offers two complementary funding opportunities for organisations creating more sustainable, inclusive and beautiful places across Europe. Whether applicants are testing new community-led approaches or delivering urban transformation in their neighbourhood in partnership with public authorities, Connect NEB and Co-create NEB support local actors in bringing the New European Bauhaus to life. Applications are open until 30 September 2026, 17.00 CEST . About the New European Bauhaus and this call The New European Bauhaus is an EU initiative that connects the European Green Deal with everyday life, supporting the creation of places that are sustainable, inclusive and beautiful . The EIT Community New European Bauhaus , led by EIT Urban Mobility in collaboration with EIT Food and Climate KIC supports local innovation, citizen engagement, entrepreneurship and place-based transformation across Europe. Through this open call, the EIT Community NEB aims to support two complementary types of local impact: Connect NEB supports community-led initiatives to test new ideas, activate local communities, and experiment with participatory approaches, living labs and new forms of governance inspired by the New European Bauhaus. Co-create NEB supports partnerships between communities, municipalities and other local actors to deliver visible, place-based transformation in public spaces. Together, the two calls help bring the New European Bauhaus to life by supporting local actors to move from ideas and participation to implementation and long-term impact. EIT funding allocation The total estimated funding available through this call is divided across two funding streams: Connect NEB and Co-create NEB . Connect NEB Each selected Connect NEB project will receive €15,300 of EIT funding, as a lump sum. The total project budget is €18,000 , including €2,700 of co-funding . Co-create NEB Each selected Co-create NEB project will receive €49,300 of EIT funding, as a lump sum. The total project budget is €58,000 , including €8,700 of co-funding . Who can apply? Connect NEB Connect NEB is a mono-beneficiary call, meaning each proposal is submitted by one organisation. It is open to single entities rooted in, or directly connected to, the territory where the project will be implemented. Co-create NEB Co-create NEB a multi-beneficiary call open to consortia of 2–4 partners. Each consortium must include at least one municipality, region, or affiliated entity. Applicants must be established in eligible countries, as defined in the Call Manual. For full eligibility requirements and special cases, applicants should refer to the Call Manual. Applicants may apply to one or both programmes but can be eligible as the Lead Partner for only one programme . For this reason, we encourage a careful review of the following sections for each programme to ensure that proposals fit the scope of the strand under which they are submitted. How can you apply? Applications must be submitted through the official EIT Urban Mobility Programmes Portal ( NetSuite ) before 30 September 2026, 17:00 CEST. Before applying, applicants are encouraged to read the Call Manual, check the eligibility requirements, download the application templates, and attend the information session. More detailed information on navigating the application form can be found in the application guidelines. https://www.eiturbanmobility.eu/call-for.text: Skip to content Home > Urban Mobility Explained (UMX) Open Call Urban Mobility Explained (UMX) Open Call 2 July 2025 EIT Urban Mobility invites organisations and experts to submit proposals to its Urban Mobility Explained (UMX) Open Call, designed to accelerate the development and delivery of high-quality, sustainable professional training and support services that close the urban mobility knowledge gap. This Call focuses on a series of specific activity areas aimed at enhancing the skills and capabilities of mobility professionals and organisations, particularly at the local/city level, to achieve systemic transformations for more liveable cities. The Call supports proposals that offer high-quality, impact-oriented, and financially sustainable learning experiences, leveraging EIT Urban Mobility’s network and expertise in various learning formats. We are seeking proposals that align with the strategic objectives of EIT Urban Mobility’s Academy, fostering innovation and entrepreneurship through a lifelong learning approach, and demonstrating potential for replication and scaling up. Emphasis is placed on courses that comply with EIT Label certification where applicable. Proposals may be submitted by individual applicants or multi-participant consortia. The following seven types of activities are eligible under this Call: CHA1: Face-to-face course(s) development and commercialisation CHA2: Face-to-face course(s) complying with the EIT Label, design and delivery CHA3: Face-to-Face course(s) complying with the EIT Label, development and commercialisation CHA4: Replicating, scaling-up, remodelling, sale of successful commercial courses and training programmes CHA5: Replicating, scaling-up, remodelling, delivery of successful EIT Label courses CHA6: Upgrading, scaling-up, remodelling of non-UMX commercial courses or repurposing non-UMX commercial courses to UMX audiences CHA7: Training operations support services and delivery for custom course pathways The Urban Mobility Explained (UMX) Open Call supports activities that demonstrate clear alignment with the strategic objectives of EIT Urban Mobility’s education and training portfolio, ensure compliance with the EIT Label requirements where applicable, and show strong potential for long-term impact, scalability, and financial sustainability. EIT funding allocation The total indicative EIT funding allocated to this Call is between approximately 2-4 million EUR. The maximum EIT funding per proposal is 700,000 EUR Who can apply? This Call for Proposals is open to all legal entities established in the Member States of the European Union, and/or in Third countries associated with Horizon Europe . These legal entities may be small and medium enterprises (SMEs), universities, research and technology organisations, cities or large businesses, among others. This Call is open to multi-participant proposals and mono-participant proposals . In the case of mono-participant proposals or multi-participant proposals involving exclusively entities from the same country, EIT Urban Mobility considers that: the pan-European dimension can be achieved by bringing participants from different countries onto the courses and exposing them to educational content that includes examples and case studies from different European countries. The instructors/ teaching staff are also expected to come from different European countries. In addition, a course in a specific city/region/country is internationalised/replicated in a different city/region/country. As such, these applicants are expected to deliver the first few sessions in a given market, and once the quality of the course has been demonstrated, it should be opened up to other markets, involving other players/partners, if needed. the knowledge triangle is integrated by involving the cities and industry partners, not only in identifying educational needs but also in designing and developing education courses in conjunction with academia. City and industry partners may also be recipients of education programmes. For information on special cases, including Switzerland and Hungarian universities, please refer to section 2.1 of the Call Manual. How can you apply? The assessment of the proposals involves two stages: Stage 1 is the expert evaluation of proposals submitted via the EIT Urban Mobility Programmes Portal (see section 4.4 of the Call Manual for submission steps), followed by Stage 2 , which includes a selection by the Selection Committee. https://www.eiturbanmobility.eu/call-for.text: Skip to content Home > RIS Education Open Call 2027 RIS Education Open Call 2027 1 June 2026 The RIS Education Open Call 2027 aims at funding projects that can support the overall RIS strategy and aims, offer high-quality education, reach a large audience and market, and gain recognition efficiently with a lasting effect. The EIT Urban Mobility RIS Education objectives are focused on capacity building in innovation and entrepreneurship and urban mobility. These objectives are reflected in the activity types proposed in this call. The activities responding to these objectives should aim to improve transferrable skills that will lead to further innovation and entrepreneurship in urban mobility in RIS countries. There are five general topics (RISE 1-5) that can be addressed by the proposals: RISE1: Capacity-Building in Innovation and Entrepreneurship RISE2: Education and Training Activities in Urban Mobility RISE3: Organisation of Winter and Summer Schools RISE4: Scaling up of Local, Regional and National Initiatives RISE5: Network building with educational players EIT funding allocation The total indicative EIT funding allocated to this call is approximately €2,600,000. Projects under RISE1 and RISE2 categories will be awarded a maximum of €300,000 EIT funding per project, whilst the maximum EIT funding per project under RIS3 will be €180,000, with maximum €90,000 per edition. For RISE4, the maximum EIT Funding per project will be €140,000 EUR and RISE5, the maximum EIT Funding will be €70,000. For more details on the financial aspects of the call, see Section 4 of the Call Manual. Who can apply? EIT Urban Mobility creates ecosystems. KICs are anchored in regional and local communities via their co-location centres (known as Innovation Hubs within EIT Urban Mobility). EIT Urban Mobility constitutes the mechanism to link the knowledge triangle components of education, research and businesses across Europe and into the wider world. At EIT Urban Mobility, we integrate these knowledge triangle components and have expanded them by adding another group: cities. Accordingly, EIT Urban Mobility currently brings together around 450 partners from 42 countries and four sectors: academia, research, industry and cities. This Call for proposals is open to all types of legal entities established in European Union (EU) member states and/or in third countries associated with Horizon Europe . These legal entities may be universities, research organisations, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), start-ups or cities, among others, and may or may not be EIT Urban Mobility partners at the time of the proposal submission. Former EIT Urban Mobility RIS Hubs and entities from Outermost Regions 1 are encouraged to apply to this Call by submitting proposals aligned with their preferred activity types. The applicants should have the expertise and previous experience in developing and implementing capacity building projects in urban mobility and/or innovation and entrepreneurship. This Call is open to both multi-participant and mono-participant proposals from one or more RIS countries. In the case of multi-participant proposals, proposals must, as a minimum requirement, be composed of at least two independent legal entities 2 from at least one RIS country. In case of mono-beneficiary proposals, the applicant must be from a RIS country. In the case of multi-participant proposals that involve entities from one country only and mono-participant proposals, the consortia shall explain how they are going to achieve the pan-European dimension in their projects. At the same time, the applying consortia are invited to integrate the knowledge triangle in their activities and should explain how cities, academia and industry partners are involved in the project design, development and implementation. How can you apply? Applications must be submitted via the EIT Urban Mobility Programmes Portal ( NetSuite ). Select the call RIS Education 2nd Open Call BP26-28. For more details on how to apply, please consult the Call Manual (section 7. Proposal submission Process) and the Guidelines for applicants. https://www.eiturbanmobility.eu/call-for.text: Skip to content Home > Master School and Fellowship Open Call 2027 Master School and Fellowship Open Call 2027 27 May 2026 EIT Urban Mobility invites universities, academic consortia, and education-focused innovators to submit proposals to its Master School and Fellowship Open Call 2027, designed to accelerate the development and delivery of high-quality learning experiences that build the skills and capabilities needed for sustainable urban mobility. This Call focuses on a series of specific activity areas aimed at meeting the objectives of the EIT Urban Mobility Master School and the EIT Urban Mobility Innovation & Entrepreneurship (I&E) Fellowship. The Call supports proposals that contribute to closing the knowledge gap within urban mobility by offering high-quality, challenge-based, intersectoral, and international education. We are seeking proposals that align with the key objectives of the Master School and I&E Fellowship, including fostering innovation and entrepreneurship skills, increasing student and graduate volumes, strengthening links to industry and cities, and supporting startup creation through EIT-labelled programmes. Proposals for the Master School and Fellowship Open Call 2027 may be submitted by individual applicants or consortia, depending on the requirements for each activity type, as detailed in the Call Manual. The following five types of activities are eligible under this Call: MSA1: Summer schools for Master students MSA2: New EIT Urban Mobility Master programmes MSA3: New universities joining the existing EIT Urban Mobility Master School programmes MSA4: I&E Master programmes that join the EIT Urban Mobility I&E Fellowship MSA5: Other educational activities contributing to KPI EITHE05.1 (startups created by students and graduates from EIT Labelled programmes) This Call supports activities that demonstrate clear alignment with the strategic objectives of EIT Urban Mobility’s education and training portfolio, ensure compliance with the EIT Label requirements and show strong potential for long-term impact, scalability, and financial sustainability. EIT funding allocation The total indicative EIT funding allocated to this Call is 1,400,000 EUR . The amounts will be allocated according to the table provided in section 4.1 of the Call Manual. Who can apply? This Call is open to organisations from the Member States of the European Union, and Third Countries associated with Horizon Europe. 1 This Call is open to multi-participant proposals or mono-participant proposals.
